London Records To Fly U.S. Distribs To 
England For New Product Sales Meet 
NEW YORK-London Record Dis- 
tributors from all key U.S. markets 
will meet in the label's namesake- 
the city of London-for a sales meet- 
ing from Jan. 5-11. 
The label has booked passage for 
more than 60 guests to attend the 
confab, which will take place in the 
new, 
ultra -modern 
Decca 
House, 
home of London's parent company, 
English Decca. 
Cash Box Names 
Rep For Spain 
FEDERICO HALPERN 
MADRID-Cash Box has named Fed- 
erico Halpern as its man in Spain. He 
will supply the magazine with a 
monthly music business column from 
that country plus a Best Sellers list. 
Halpern entered the Spanish disk 
scene in 1959, beginning with a re- 
view column in a weekly magazine 
about films 
and 
music. 
He 
also 
started two deejay programs with 
records culled from the international 
market. 
He left radio work to start, in 
April, 1962, the only magazine in 
Spain devoted exclusively to records, 
Discobolo, of which he is now techni- 
cal manager and editor. His initial 
work for Cash Box was the Spanish 
year-end wrap-up in 
the Dec. 28 
special. 
C/P-Robinson Deal 
NEW YORK-An agreement has 
been reached between Cameo -Park- 
way Records and Harold Robinson 
for future releases on the Parkway 
label of all Robinson disks, including 
those by Patty LaBelle & The Blue - 
belles, a recent chart attraction with 
"Down 
The Aisle" 
on 
Robinson's 
Nicetown label. First deck under the 
deal is the gals' follow-up to their 
hit, a reading of "You'll Never Walk 
Alone." Robinson will produce the 
team's sides for Parkway. He's dis- 
continuing the operation of Nicetown. 
Patty & The Bluebelles had a top hit 
awhile back in "I Sold My Heart To 
The Junkman."

A contingent of London execs- 
headed by D. H. Toller -Bond, exec 
veep, will accompany the guests, who 
will be given a preview of London's 
Jan. releases, which 
include 
pop, 
classical, phase 4 and international 
diskings. 
Also on the schedule of events are: 
a tour of British Decca's vast net- 
work of manufacturing plants and 
recording studios; demonstrations of 
new recording equipment by Arthur 
Haddy, hifi expert and pioneer of 
London's famed sound; and a social 
itenerary including the theatre and

The gathering will be capped -off 
by a black -tie dinner at the Mayfair 
Hotel. 
As part of the presentation of new 
product, London will utilize the tal- 
ents of its stars, including Mantovani, 
Ted Heath, Edmundo Ros and Johnny 
Keating, who will introduce their own 
new product. 
Decca Sets Sales Meet 
For N.Y., Hollywood 
NEW YORK-Decca Records holds 
two sales meets this week (30) in 
New York and Hollywood to acquaint 
the company's divisional sales force 
with the label's mid -winter product 
and plans. 
Along with new product for dealer 
re -stocking, the district sales force 
will also be introduced to the addition 
of three new phono models in a popu- 
lar price range. 
The home office delegation to the 
New York meeting will be led by Syd 
N. Goldberg, Decca's veep in charge 
of national sales, while the west coast 
contingent will be headed by Claude 
Brennan. 
Meets will take place as the label 
reports one of its strongest selling 
periods in recent history. 
Ben -Ven To Cut Hodges 
For Releases On MGM 
NEW YORK-Eddie Hodges moves 
over to the MGM label via a deal with 
Nick Venet-Fred Benson indie pro- 
duction outfit, Ben -Ven Productions. 
Hodges, who had 
a number of 
successful teen -market singles, has 
inked an exclusive pact with Ben -Ven, 
which also has an indie deal with 
MGM. He'll be in the studio this week 
for a release a short while later. 
On the Cadence label, the 17 -year - 
old singer -actor had such clicks as 
"I'm Gonna Knock On Your Door," 
Bandit of My Dreams" and "(Girls, 
Girls, Girls) Made to Love." After his 
Cadence stint, he cut for Columbia 
Records. 
Decca Opens Its 
Own Branch In Memphis 
NEW YORK-Decca Records' 20th 
company -owned distrib branch has 
been opened in Memphis, according to 
Syd Goldberg, veep and general sales 
manager. 
For the past decade, the Decca 
Coral and Brunswick labels have been 
previously distributed in the city by 
the Stratton -Warren Co. 
Goldberg 
said that the existing sales organiza- 
tion in Memphis will remain intact as 
a company -owned branch under the 
direction of 
sales manager 
Jack 
Brown. 
Branch officially opens its doors for 
business this Thurs. (2) at 668 S. 
Main St. 
Eight Red Seals 
In Victor Jan. Rel. 
NEW YORK-RCA Victor has an- 
nounced the release of eight Red Seal 
albums for Jan. 
The new issue includes "Falla: El 
Amor Brujo and Berlioz: Les Nuits 
D'Ete" with Leontyne Price, Fritz 
Reiner and the Chicago Symphony 
Orchestra; 
Mozart's 
"Piano 
Con- 
certo No. 20" with Artur Rubinstein 
and orchestra conducted by Alfred 
Wallenstein; 
Mozart's 
"Symphony 
No. 41" and "Eine Kleine Nacht- 
musik" with the Boston Symphony 
Orchestra conducted by Erich Leins- 
dorf; 
"Popular Classics For 
The 
Spanish Guitar" with Julian Bream; 
Eric Friedman with the London Sym- 
phony Orchestra conducted by Mal- 
colm Sargent; and "Women In My 
Life" by Sergio Franchi. 
MGM Signs 
Hank Williams, Jr. 
HANK WILLIAMS, 
JR. 
NEW YORK-Hank Williams, Jr., 
son of the late, great singer -writer, 
has entered the disk scene on MGM 
Records, the label that cut his father. 
The 14 -year -old performer will be- 
gin his disk career with a single fea- 
turing, "Long Gone Lonesome Blues," 
which the senior Williams wrote and 
recorded. Young Williams was sched- 
uled to sing the tune on last Sunday's 
Ed Sullivan TV'er. MGM is releasing 
the side this week. 
The artist is being managed by 
his mother, Audrey Williams, and is 
being booked through the William 
Morris Agency. He has appeared in a 
flick, 
"Hollywood 
on 
Broadway," 
which was 
produced 
by 
Audrey 
Williams. 
Hank Williams died on New Year's 
Day 1953, with his many recorded 
efforts 
continuing 
to 
be 
among 
MGM's top -selling items in LP form. 
Andy Williams Forms 
Indie Producing Firm 
BEVERLY 
HILLS, 
CALIF.-Andy 
Williams has formed his own indie 
production company for disks, TV and 
motion pictures under the name of 
Barnaby Productions. Alan Bernard, 
the star's manager, is veep of the 
operation. The singer has just con- 
cluded a banner sales year for the Co- 
lumbia label with both singles and 
LP successes. 
Mercury Pacts 
Jerry Wallace 
HOLLYWOOD-Jerry Wallace 
has 
been signed to a long-term contract 
at Mercury Records. 
Wallace, inked by Jack Tracy, the 
label's west coast director, will cut his 
first sides for the label this week. 
On the Challenge label, the song- 
ster came through with such chart 
items as "Primrose Lane," his first 
hit, "How The Time Flies," and "Shut- 
ters & Boards." 
Motown's '64 Expansion 
Plans Include C&W 
And Comedy Disks 
DETROIT-Berry Gordy, Jr., presi- 
dent of Motown Records, has an- 
nounced a series of moves on the 
part of the company aimed at cap- 
turing a greater share of the total 
record market. 
According to Gordy, the company 
will step up its activities in the area 
of pop music, country, western and 
folk. In addition, the company will 
release a number of comedy albums 
next year. 
Barney Ales, vice president of Mo- 
town Sales Corp., said that the com- 
pany has signed former child singing 
star Bobby Breen for the pop field 
and that motion -picture funnyman 
Stephin' Fetchit is currently complet- 
ing a comedy album for release early 
in 1964. 
The Melody label, which involves 
country, western and folk music, is 
being bolstered with the addition of 
singers Bruce Channel of "Hey Baby" 
fame, Howard Crockett and Gene 
Henslee. Responsibility for records on 
this label rests with Al Klien, who 
operates the company's southwestern 
office in Dallas, Texas. 
In commenting on the move Ales 
said: "The addition of these stars is 
one part of a long range plan at Mo- 
town. We intend to maintain our po- 
sition in the popular market and to 
move into the areas of spoken word 
albums, broadway cast albums and 
speciality material." 
"Disque" Clubs Budding In U.S. 
NEW YORK-A popular form of Eu- 
ropean nitery entertainment - disk 
playing for dancing-is making some 
headway in the U.S. 
One New York club, The Village 
Vanguard, the popular jazz attraction, 
recently began spinning of disks- 
complete with "deejay"-recently be- 
gan spinning of disks-complete with 
"deejay"-to draw late -hour dancers. 
Now out on the west coast, the 
"Whiskey Disque" will premiere on 
Los Angeles' Sunset Strip Jan. 15, 
according to owner Shelly Davis. 
Formerly called The Party, the 
club was recently purchased by Davis 
and partners of the Strip's Crescendo 
and Interlude clubs. 
Said to be the first west coast 
nitery to intersperse "live" and auto- 
mated entertainment, the club is in- 
stalling more than $10,000 worth of 
stereo sound equipment and speaker 
systems as well as remodeling the 
main room to meet acoustical consid- 
erations. 
In addition, the club will have life- 
like, animated replicas of musicians 
that will provide "an authentic at- 
mosphere for dancing to recorded mu- 
sic," Davis said. 
Davis said he was arranging with 
leading diskeries to an "extensive" 
record library to be kept at the club. 
The club's disk -playing policy will 
be: as the club will be open until 4 an) 
every night, it will play dance music 
until 2 am, new comedy records until 
closing. 
This form of nitery-disk entertain- 
ment has caught -on in Paris, Rome 
and other Continental cities plus somE 
areas of South America.

New Belair Post 
For Phillippe Boutet 
NEW YORK-During a visit to the 
Cash Box offices last week, Phillippe 
Boutet announced his appointment as 
assistant to Nicole Barclay, head of 
Belair Records and several publishing 
firms in France. 
Boutet will be in the U.S. for sev- 
eral weeks for a series of business 
meetings here and on the West Coast.

"LOOK WHO'S SURFIN' NOW"-Various Art- 
ists-King 882 
Here's a lively, high-powered set featuring a host 
of name artists including James Brown, King 
Curtis and Freddy King reading a bevy of dance- 
able surfin' tunes. The performers obviously have 
their eyes out for teen acceptance as the pro- 
gram consists of the rhythmic, strong -beat vari- 
ety of the west coast -based music. Fine listening 
throughout. 
"SLAPPY WHITE AT THE CLUB HARLEM"- 
Chess LP1481 
Slappy White proves himself an easy-going and 
glib purveyor of humor on this "live" recording 
from the Club Harlem on Chess. The comic is 
primarily a storyteller and he draws from any 
and all facets of society for his material. He 
pokes harmless fun at integration, teenagers, 
sex, Castro and a diversity of other current top- 
ics. Plent of laffs to be had here. 
"HOT RODS-U.S.A."-Battle 6131 
The latest rage sweeping the nation from the 
west coast is the hot craze. Although an entire 
body of music is associated with the trend, there 
is also interest in the racing itself. This interest- 
ing, off -beat Battle disk features the actual 
sounds of some of the top hot-rodders around to- 
day racing on various drag strips around the 
U.S. Everything from the sound of the crowds to 
the harsh noise of the engines is captured on the 
album. 
"JACK 
ELLIOTT 
SINGS THE SONGS OF 
WOODY GUTHRIE"-Prestige FL 14011 
The countless folk songs composed by legendary 
Woody Guthrie make up a significant portion of 
the contemporary American folk tradition. Jack 
Elliott pays a musical tribute to Guthrie by offer- 
ing a tasteful program of some of Guthrie's 
better-known tunes. Highlights of the disk in- 
clude "Hard Travellin'," "New York Town" and 
"This Land Is Your Land." Superior listening 
throughout. 
"HOOTENANNY FOR ORCHESTRA" - Walter 
Raim-Liberty LST 7332 
Who sez folk music has to be played by small, 
often un -musical groups and performers? Cer- 
tainly not Walter Raim who has arranged a bevy 
of popular folk items for full ork on this pleasant 
new offering from Liberty. The talented Raim 
doubles as a conductor as he leads the band in 
top-drawer readings of "All My Trails," "East 
Virginia" and "Over The Hills." 
"THE DANCIN'EST BAND AROUND" - Leon 
McAuliffe-Capitol ST 2016 
Leon McAuliffe and his Cimarron Boys kick off 
their Capitol careers with this delightful disk of 
country -western material. 
The program here 
"Four 
all the way from standards like 
Walls" to recent chart clicks like "The Tips Of 
My Fingers." The orkster's own distinctive sound 
makes for top-notch dancing or listening pleasure. 
"SING OUT AMERICA"-Tell Tale Singers- 
Aravel AB 1001 
One of the by-products of the current folk music 
craze is the appearance of countless new groups 
and artists. This new Aravel set showcases the 
versatile vocal and instrumental talents of a new 
group called the Tell Tale Singers. The crew dis- 
plays loads of poise and sensitive understanding 
of the folk idiom as they offer "Midnight Spe- 
cial," "I Never Will Marry" and "Banks Of The 
Ohio."

"THE ESSENTIAL COLEMAN HAWKINS" - 
Verve V 8568 
Coleman Hawkins easily ranks high in jazzdom's 
inner circle on the basis of his amazing staying 
power. For almost thirty years the saxist has 
excited new generations of jazz -lovers with his 
melodic, lyrical soulful approach to music. On this 
fine Verve date Hawkins really swings on 
"There's A Small Hotel," "Body And Soul" and 
"How Long Has This Been Going On." 
JAll BEST BETS 
"JUST JAZZ!"-Various Artists-Imperial LP 
9246 
Here's a delightful program spotlighting the di- 
verse and distinctive talents of such fine jazz 
artists as Erroll Garner, Lester Young, Billie 
Holiday, John Coltrane and Paul Chambers. The 
set has something for everyone running the 
gamut from Garner's easy-going swing -style jazz, 
"White Rose Bounce," to Coltrane's highly -per- 
sonal, new -wave musical representations, "Visi- 
tation." Disk should appeal to a wide variety of 
j azzophiles. 
"DONALD BYRD AT THE HALF NOTE CAFE" 
-Blue Note -4061 
With each new Blue Note LP trumpeter Donald 
Byrd gets significantly better and this set cut 
live at New York's Blue Note Cafe is no excep- 
tion to the rule. While backed by a fine crew of 
jazzmen including Pepper Davis (baritone sax), 
Dyke Pearson (piano), Laymon Jackson (bass) 
and Lex Humphries (drums), Byrd wails superb- 
ly in his own distinctive swingin' midstream 
style. Best listening bets here are "My Girl 
Shirl," "A Portrait Of Jennie" and "When Sonny 
Gets Blue." 
"THE JOE DALEY TRIO AT NEWPORT '63" 
-RCA Victor LSP 2763 
Although the annual Newport Jazz Festival is 
usually associated with jazzdom's big, somewhat 
conservative names, avanta-garde groups are 
also presented with equal fervor, The Joe Daley 
Trio, which scored a triumph at the last fete, is 
one such new -wave combo. On this premiere ses- 
sion the boys turn in some first-rate musically 
sophisticated performances on "Ballad," "One 
Note" and "Ramblin." 
CLASSICAL PICKS 
COMEIVOIMEISICIMPII, u OCIEWIENI 
"N ÍVÌ 
STRAUSS: Don Quixote, Philadelphia Orch/Or- 
mandy-Columbia ML 5915 
The Philadelphia Orchestra, with Eugene Or- 
mandy at the helm, performs Richard Strauss' 
tone poem, "Don Quixote" with viola solo by 
Carlton Cooley and cello solo by Lorne Munroe. 
The complex orchestral structure includes an in- 
troduction, a main theme with ten variations and 
a finale and is executed by the orchestra and 
conductor with brilliance and sensitivity. The opus 
is one of the composer's finest works and this 
performance is a worthy addition to the classical 
shelf. 
MOZART: Complete Wind Music Vol. 1, London 
Wind Soloists/Brymer-London CS6346 
Jack Brymer conducts the London Wind Soloists, 
and also doubles as clarinetist, on a series of 
Mozart compositions for wind instruments. In- 
cluded here are Largo, Menuetto, Adagio, Menu - 
etto, (allegretto), Romanza, Tema con veriazioni, 
and Rondo. These selections played by the 13 - 
piece group reflect the quiet dignity of a chamber 
group without being bound by the same limita- 
tions. Top-notch classical fare. 
VIVALDI: Four Concerti - Nathan Milstein, 
violinist-Angel S 36004 
Nathan Milstein needs no introduction to classical 
record -buyers. The talented violinist has already 
earned countless critical kudos through the years 
for his first-rate performances. On this new An- 
gel outing of four Vivaldi concerti, Milstein 
further elevates his reputation by rendering the 
intricate, complex strains of the various works 
with all of his expected poise and artistry. Clas- 
sical fans should come out in droves for this one.

Teen Queen 
HOLLYWOOD-A typewriter, $500 
in cash and a date with Jimmy Gil- 
mer. These are the gifts awarded to 
"Teen Queen" Miss Diane Martin of 
Los Angeles after her election on a 
special "Queen For A Day" program 
broadcast last week on ABC-TV. In 
the above pic the Teen Queen is 
flanked by Dot's Jimmy Gilmer, cur-

Petal Pickin'," and Jack Bailey emcee 
of the show. 
Milva To Debut In U.S. 
NEW 
YORK-Italian 
songstress 
Milva will make her American debut 
at Carnegie Hall on Jan. 18 and at 
the Academy of Music in Brooklyn on 
the 19th. 
Milva achieved her first recogni- 
tion at the 1961 San Remo Song 
Festival and has since gone on to 
score in the top three of every Italian 
festival. The lark records for Cetra 
in Italy and has 15 singles and 15 
LP's on the market. She will remain 
in the U.S. for two weeks.

has issued a new single by British 
songstress Shirley Bassey tagged, 
"My Special Dream" backed with 
"How Can You Tell?" 
The "Dream" side is an adaptation 
of one of the themes from Carl Fore- 
man's flick, "The Victors."

"LOVE WALKED IN" - Andre Previn - RCA 
Camden CAS 792 
The multi -faceted Andre Previn showcases his 
amazing keyboard style in the pop idiom on 
this swingin' set from RCA Camden. The 88'er 
does not resort to tricks or stylistic gimmicks 
but renders each item in a straightforward, high- 
ly -skilled manner. While backed by a subtle ork, 
Previn turns in outstanding renditions of "Who's 
Sorry Now," "Love Walked In" and "Thinking 
Of You." 
"ALIKI-MY LOVE" - Original Soundtrack - 
Fontana MGF 27523 
Manos (Never On Sunday) Hadjidakis could have 
another film -track winner with this delightful 
and lilting "Aliki-My Love" score. Although there 
is no individual tune that stands out as did the 
"Never On Sunday" hit, "The Magic Isle (The 
Wedding Song)" could vie for singles honors. 
The bright, airy score is thoroughly engaging 
and effective. Impressive bands are "Aliki," "The 
Villagers Serenade" and "Aliki's Cha Cha." 
"THE BEST OF STAN FREBERG" - Capitol 
T2020 
Stan Freberg recreates a dozen of his famous 
satirical and comic parodies on this new release 
from Capitol. Most of the items here pulled 
plenty of coin the first time out and could again. 
The laffman's legions of fans will get plenty of 
chuckles as he delivers, "The Yellow Rose of 
Texas," "St. George And The Dragonet" and 
"Banana Boat." Plenty of fun listening to be 
had here. 
"Y CANCIONES 
DE PEDRO FLORES"-EI 
Trio Los Panchos-Columbia ES 1811 
The Trio Los Panchos have made significant in- 
roads in the Latin markets with their previous 
Columbia albums and this new romantic entry 
ranks as a worthy addition to their catalog. The 
group's distinctive style of harmony and effec- 
tive counterpoint is firmly evidenced on "Que 
Te Pasa," "Amor Perdido" and "Bajo Un Palmar 
Tranquilo." Loads of potential here. 
"MORE OF TRINI LOPEZ"-King 877 
Trini Lopez, who skyrocketed to international 
prominence last year with two best-selling albums 
on another label, serves up a dozen rock and 
roll items and ballads on this session during 
his tenure with King. The chanter -guitarist pre- 
sents a variety of moods and tempos here as 
he feelingfully reads his way thru such items 
as "Yes You Do," "Don't Treat Me That Way" 
and "Rock On." Album could score in sales and 
airplay. 
"40 FAVORITE JEWISH MELODIES"-David 
Herzel-Request SRLP 10055 
Here is a top-drawer package of Jewish melodies 
on Request played by The Music League Of 
Tel Aviv under the direction of David Herzl. 
A large orchestra, complete with loads of lush 
strings, adapts symphonic -like arrangements for 
these familiar tunes. Included here are superb 
renditions of such favorites as "Havah Nagilah," 
"Bin Ich Mir A Schnaiderl," "Jewish Brigade 
Song," and "Shalom Cha'verim." 
"STRANGE TRUTHS"-Tom O'Neil-Petal 3000 
Tom O'Neil comes up with volume two of his 
"Strange Truths" series on the Petal label. As 
in volume one, O'Neil narrates a series of tales 
of psychic phenomena and the supernatural ex- 
perienced by real people. On this set the creator 
tells of "Countess De Armil's Spirit Voices," 
"Lady Londonberry's 13th Guest," "Ralph Bell- 
amy's Hunches," "A Ghost Convicts His Mur- 
derer" and many others.

"TOGETHER AGAIN"-Benny Goodman Quartet 
-RCA LSP 2698 
The legendary original Benny Goodman Quartet 
consisting of Goodman, Lionel Hampton, Gene 
Krupa and Teddy Wilson is re -united on this 
top-drawer swingin' set from RCA Victor. Al- 
though all the members of the group have gone 
their different ways during the past twenty-five 
years, they still have the ability to form one 
cohesive musical unit. The group shines on "Seven 
Come Eleven," "I've Found A New Baby" and 
"Who Cares." Jazzophiles should really dig it. 
"THE SYMPHONIC ELLINGTON"-Duke Ell- 
ington-Reprise R9-6097 
Duke Ellington and his orchestra play four ex- 
tended Ellington compositions supported at times 
by the symphony and opera orchestras of Paris, 
Hamburg, Stockholm and La Scala, Milan. On 
this new album outing on Reprise, the jazz 88'er 
also serves as composer and conductor as he 
reads his way through "Night Creature," "Non - 
Violent Integration," "La Scala, She Too Pretty 
To Be Blue" and "Harlem." Jazzophiles will 
probably dig it. 
"SOUL SHACK"-Sonny Stitt/Jack McDuff- 
Prestige PR7297 
Sonny Stitt, an outspoken exponent of swing 
jazz, and Jack McDuff team up on Prestige on 
a set of tunes both old and new, but all done 
in a swingin' tempo. The saxist and the organist 
get top-flight assistance from Leonard Gaskin on 
bass and Herbie Lovelle on drums here as they 
bounce through such goodies as "Sunday," "Soul 
Shack," "Love Nest" and "For You." A very 
enjoyable jazz package. 
JAll BEST BETS 
"THE ESSENTIAL DIZZY GILLESPIE"-Verve 
V 8586 
For over two decades Dizzy Gillespie has re- 
mained firmly in his niche as one of jazzdom's 
leaders. On this Verve outing, the trumpeter, 
backed by both small combo and big band, dis- 
plays his inventive, swingin' style on a group 
of tunes long associated with him. Gillespie 
creates some valid melodic developments on "Ex- 
actly Like You," "Sometimes I'm Happy" and 
"A Night In Tunisia." 
"UNA MAS"-Kenny Dorham-Blue Note 4127 
At a time when jazz is in danger of resorting to 
conformist patterns, ace trumpeter Kenny Dor- 
ham stands as dramatic proof -positive that there 
is still a place for originality. On this Blue Note 
set Dorham is teamed -up with an accomplished 
crew of jazzmen including Joe Henderson and 
Herbie Hancock. The trumpeter wails in his 
potent, hard -driving lyrical style on "Una Mas," 
"Straight Ahead" and "Sao Paulo." A splendid 
achievement. 
CLASSICAL PICKS 
"BIRGIT NILSSON IN AIDA" - London OS 
25798 
Birgit Nilsson performs the principal arias from 
Verdi's classic work, "Aida," on this potent disk 
from London. The soprano, supported by a cast 
that includes Grace Hoffman, Luigi Ottollm, 
Louis Quilico and the Orchestra of the Royal 
Opera House, Covent Garden, conducted by John 
Pritchard, superbly handles the role of Aida as 
she gives emotional depth and lyrical beauty 
to the role. Opera buffs will surely like it. 
BEETHOVEN: Fidelio, Various Artists, Ferenc 
Fricsay/Conductor-Deutsche Grammophon 
138 
390/91 
Ludwig Von Beethoven's opera "Fidelio" is per- 
formed by a host of renowned international art- 
ists and the Bavarian State Orchestra and Chorus 
conducted by Ferenc Fricsay and Alfred Leder. 
The title role is sung by Leonie Rysanek sup- 
ported by such notables as Dietrich -Fischer- 
" 
Dieskau, Ernst Hafliger and Irmgard Seefried: 
The performers are faithful and sensitive In 
their interpretations. A first-rate operatic offering 
from DGG.

Ace Now On Bootlegging 
In Orient, Weiss Says 
NEW YORK-Considering the yearly 
disk sales in the Orient, bootlegging 
of American disks and non -authorized 
use of American music copyrights can 
no longer be disregarded. 
This is the opinion of Bobby Weiss, 
former international man for Warner 
Bros. Records (now on his own), who 
spoke to a luncheon gathering of the 
International Record and Music Men's 
Club last Thurs. (9). 
Weiss reported that the combined 
annual sales total in Japan, Hong 
Kong, the Philippines, South Vietnam, 
Thailand 
and 
Singap re/Malaysia 
amounted 
to 
$56,539,939 
in 
1962 
(based in local manufacturing plus 
certain imports). 
Disk purchasers in the Orient, Weiss 
declared, are eager to take advantage 
of bogus disks since their earnings 
do not let them afford the relatively 
high prices for disks in the area 
(singles prices vary from 50¢ in the 
Philippines to $1 in Japan, LP's in 
the same territories go from $3.60 to 
$5). 
Weiss termed Taiwan the "hub of 
the record pirate industry" in the 
Orient and declared that the situation 
there puts the entire record and music 
industry in the Orient in "peril." He 
said that Taiwan is exporting about 
$250,000 worth of bogus 
disks a 
month. 
While he noted that RIAA, the disk 
industry association in the U.S., was 
attempting to do something about the 
situation, the Taiwan Govt. has not 
been strict in enforcing its declared 
drive against such practices. 
"Think about-but more important 
-write your Senator, write your 
Govt. and let them know that this 
type of piracy is helping deprive you 
of income-and more than that, our 
support of the Taiwan/Formosa gov- 
ernment against Communist China- 
with millions of dollars-should be 
sufficient compensation without their 
record companies resorting to piracy." 
Weiss also enumerated many other 
pirating practices in the Orient, in- 
cluding unauthorized use of lyric 
sheets of U.S. tunes in the sleeves of 
singles in Japan, trans -shipping in 
Hong Kong on an export level (Weiss 
said that Hong Kong was the "biggest 
trans -shipping market of them all") 
and other practices that cut into the 
income of U.S. disk men and publish- 
ers. 
"A continuous observation of the 
Oriental scene," Weiss concluded, "is 
all-important to our ever-growing in- 
ternational record/music business- 
as the Orient is the next key record 
music market-this I can assure you." 
Amy -Mala To Issue 
Lou Johnson Releases 
NEW YORK-Larry Uttal, general 
manager of Amy -Mala Records, has 
announced the signing of an agree- 
ment with the Aberbach group for the 
distribution of all future Lou Johnson 
releases. The disks will be issued on 
the Hilltop label and distributed by 
Amy -Mala. 
Johnson, who recently scored with 
"Reach Out For Me," will be released 
under the new set-up on a new Burt 
Bacharach-produced single titled "It 
Ain't No Use."

NEW 
YORK-The 
Jamie/Guyden 
Dist. Co. has taken over the national 
distribution of the LeCam label of 
Ft. Worth, Texas. First release under 
the deal is Bruce Channel's "Going 
Back To Louisiana." Several years 
ago, the songster gave the Smash 
label a hit side with "Hey Baby."

"BOB NEWHART FACES BOB NEWHART"- 
Warner Bros. 1517 
Bob Newhart scored a series of chart triumphs 
with his first several Warner Bros. albums and 
makes a strong bid for similar status with this 
new comedy outing. The laffman's flair for get- 
ting to the heart of comic situations and people is 
much in evidence here as he humorously talks 
about a "Nudist Camp Expose," "The Expectant 
Father" and "On Poodles And Planes." The hu- 
morist's new material and potent delivery could 
spark sales for the LP. 
"THE BRANDYWINE SINGERS"-Joy JL 1000 
Once in a great while a new pop -folk group comes 
on the scene which deserves special attention. 
The Brandywine Singers are such a group. The 
youthful artists display a keen understanding of 
folk material and moving sensitivity as they go 
through their paces with verve and polish. Best 
listening bets here are "Two Little Boys," "Sat- 
urday's Child" and "Two -Ten, Six -Eighteen." 
"ADIEU, LITTLE SPARROW"-Edith Piaf- 
Philips PCC208 
The late Edith Piaf's countless admirers through- 
out the world will surely want to own this collec- 
tion of songs issued on Philips Connoisseur series. 
The bookfold jacket includes biographical notes 
on the life of the famed French singer. The songs 
here are laden with the emotional depth and trag- 
edy that were Piaf's trademarks. Memorable 
tracks are "My Legionnaire," "On The Other Side 
Of The Street," "She Could Be Found On The 
Rue Pigalle" and "Broken Record." A potent en- 
try. 
"TRAIN TIME"-Erik Darling-Vanguard VRS 
9131 
Stepping out of his role as the leader of the Roof- 
top Singers, Erik Darling goes the solo route on 
this top-drawer Vanguard session of folk and 
blues items. While accompanying himself on the 
6 and 12 -string guitar and banjo, the chanter's 
rich, wild -range voice carries him in good stead 
as he turns in superb versions of "Hail John," 
"Train Time" and "I Love My Love." All of the 
artist's many fans should come out in force for 
the LP. 
"ANNETTE ON CAMPUS"-Vista 3320 
Annette, who made substantial chart inroads with 
her recent "Beach Party" issue makes the grand 
tour of the country's colleges and universities and 
introduces the Wellingtons and the All-American 
Chorus on the many college songs included here. 
The lark's vocal contributions are insignificant 
but the two choral groups come through with ex- 
uberance. Bill of fare includes "On Brave Old 
Army Team," "Yale Boola," "On Wisconsin" and 
Many others. 
"BLUE MARTINI"-John Neel/Plas Johnson- 
Ava 24 
John Neel doubles as composer and conductor 
with Plas Johnson providing the tenor sax solos 
and arrangements on this pop session on Ava. 
The melodies are blues -oriented and the sounds 
lush with strings and reeds. The composer com- 
bines pop with a jazz flavor in a series of easy - 
paced tunes. Best bets here are "Blue Martini," 
"Once Upon A Blues" and "Only The Blues." 
Pleasant late -hours mood companion. 
"HAP PEEBLES PRESENTS COUNTRY MU- 
SIC U.S.A."-Various Artists-Starday SLP 263 
For over thirty years the name Hap Peebles has 
been as closely tied to country music as ham to 
eggs. This top-flight Starday disk, cut live at a 
recent Peebles presentation in Kansas City, fea- 
tures such well-known c&w luminaries as Minnie 
Pearl, Dick Flood, The Plainsmen, Moon Mulli- 
can, George Jones, delivering a bevy of popular 
tunes and comedy routines. Album should rack 
up healthy returns.

"WOODY HERMAN: 1964"-Philips PHS 600. 
118 
The amazing thing about the Woody Herman 
band is their staying power. The group has been 
swingin' up a storm for over twenty-five years 
and shows no indication of letting up in intensity. 
On this new Philips set the gang renders a bevy 
of all -favorites and newer items all played in 
their distinctive, easy-going, relaxed style. Best 
listening bets here include "Deep Purple," "After 
You've Gone" and "My Wish." 
"BOLA SETE AND FRIENDS"-Vince Guaraldi 
-Fantasy 3356 
Here's a delightful musical marriage spotlighting 
the distinctive musical talents of the Bola Sete 
group with 
Vince 
Guaraldi. 
Neither 
artist 
changes his style or perspective for the other. 
Instead the two jazzmen compliment each other 
as they turn in superlative renditions of "Days 
Of Wine And Roses," "Star Song" and "Moon 
Rays." Loads of sales potential here. 
"THE ESSENTIAL ANDRE PREVIN"-Verve 
V 8565 
In the short span of a decade Andre Previn has 
earned the reputation as one of the most multi- 
talented musicians around. On this Verve disk 
the jazz side of the Previn coin is spotlighted in a 
compelling collection of self -penned instrumental 
favorites. Previn, who arranged the selections, is 
showcased on the 88 as he reads "Like Young," 
"Little Girl Blue" and "Young Man's Lament." 
Jazzophiles should really dig it. 
JAll BEST BETS 
"ONE STEP BEYOND"-Jackie McLean-Blue 
Note 4137 
The tag of this new Jackie McLean set aptly de. 
scribes the avant-garde musical expression on 
this lively disk. The alto saxist is backed by a fine 
group of jazzmen here including Grachan Moncur 
(trombone), Bobby Hutcherson (vibes) and Eddie 
Kahan (bass) as he goes through his swingin' 
inventive paces in his expected highly -personal 
fashion. Jackie and the boys really shine on "Sat- 
urday And Sunday," "Frankenstein" and "Ghost 
Town." 
"THE BEST OF WOODY HERMAN"-Everest 
5222 
Woody Herman has fused his old big -band hits 
with a modern jazz flavor on this swinging ses- 
sion on Everest. When the clarinetist did these 
tunes the first time around they became swing 
classics and have since gone on to be jazz classics. 
"The Woodchopper's Ball," "Caldonia," "Lulla- 
by Of Birdland" and "Midnight Sun" are included 
in the set. The fans will dig the disk. 
CLASSICAL PICKS 
MOZART: Jupiter Symphony, Eine Kleine Nacht. t 
musik, Boston Symph. Orch/Leinsdorf-RCA Vic' 
tor LM2694 
The Boston Symphony Orchestra, with Erich 
Leinsdorf at the helm, brilliantly performs Mo- 
zart's final symphony, the Jupiter, and his lilting- 
ly melodic Eine Kleine Nachtmusik on this superb 
classical offering from RCA Victor. The maestros 
interpretation is faultless and the orchestra su- 
preme. The classical devotee will enjoy 
the 
breath -taking fourth movement as well as the 
immensely popular "Nachtmusik" serenade. 
BRAHMS: Alto Rhapsody; Mildred Miller, mew. - 
soprano; Bruno Walter conducting the Columbia 
Symphony-Columbia ML 5888 
Here's a superb classical offering featuring the 
late Bruno Walter conducting the Columbia Sym- 
phony Orchestra and Mildred Miller (mezzo -s° 
prano) in a beautiful program of Brahms and 
Mahler works. In addition to the ork, the disk 
boasts the Occidental College Concert Choir on 
some of the tracks. Walter's reading is extremely 
lyrical and underlines the basic romantic theme= 
of the various selections. A standout achieve- 
ment.

Atco Is Distributing 
Single On Amanda 
NEW YORK-Ateo Records has ar- 
ranged with George Hudson, owner of 
Amanda Records, to handle the na- 
tional distribution of the single, "I 
Have 
A Dream" by the Hudson 
Chorale. The disk will remain under 
the Amanda banner. 
Jerry Wexler, Ateo vice president, 
said that a share of the royalties from 
the disk would be turned over to Rev. 
Martin Luther King for his Southern 
Christian Leadership Conference. 
The tune, inspired by King's famous 
"I Have A Dream" speech, was writ- 
ten by Hudson, a Newark deejay and 
an authority on gospel music.

BERT KEMPFERT"-Epic LN 24080 
Bobby Hackett offers a musical tribute to Bert 
Kaempfert on this melodic set of tunes made pop. 
ular by the vet orkster. The trumpeter gives each 
selection his individual, distinctive attention as he 
goes through his paces with all of his expected 
poise and verve. Hackett shines on "Wonderland 
By Night," "Now And Forever" and "Sunday In 
Madrid." Fine fare for either dancing or listen- 
ing pleasure. 
"BROTHER JACK AT THE JAZZ WORKSHOP 
LIVE!"-Jack McDuff-Prestige 7286 
Jack McDuff's first in -person LP on Prestige, 
"Live!" pulled plenty of coin for the organist and 
this new session cut live at the Jazz Workshop is 
sure to meet with the same wide acceptance. Mc 
Duff is modern without being extreme and tradi- 
tional without seeming square and the seven 
bands here are geared for universal appeal. Bright 
tracks here are "Blues 1 & 8," "Grease Monkey,' 
"Vas Dis" and "Jive Samba." Heavy sales arc 
indicated. 
JAll BEST BETS 
"TOBACCO ROAD"-Lou Rawls-Capitol ST 2042 
With each new album Lou Rawls significantly 
gains in stature and poise. On this new set the 
blues songster displays an emotional power and 
conviction never evidenced on his previous record- 
ings. While backed by a full Onzy Matthews- 
helmed ork, Rawls offers some poignant readings 
of "Tobacco Road," "Cotton Fields" and "Blue: 
For A Four String Guitar." LP should create 
plenty of excitement. 
"A NEW PERSPECTIVE"-Donald Byrd-Blue 
Note 4124 
Here's an off -beat, interesting set coupling the 
midstream jazz artistry of trumpeter Donald 
Byrd with an eight -voice chorus and band. Byrd 
does not attempt to blend in with the band and 
chorus. Instead, he makes his highly -personal mu- 
sical statements which, in a lyrical sense, compli- 
ments the other happenings on the disk. Standout 
cuts here are "Elijah," "Best Of Burden" and 
"The Black Disciple." Pleasant late -hours mood 
companion. 
"COMIN' IN THE BACK DOOR"-Wynton Kelly 
-RCA Victor V 8576 
Ace jazz 88'er Wynton Kelly teams up with an 
accomplished group of musicians including Kenny 
Burrell (guitar), Paul Chambers (bass) and Jim- 
my Cobb (drums) on this delightful swingin' free - 
flowing Victor outing. Kelly does not resort to 
gimmicks but renders each item in an amazingly 
honest fashion. Among the most enjoyable tracks 
are "Don't Wait To Long," "The Bitter End" and 
"To Kill A Mockingbird." Superior listening 
throughout. 
CLASSICAL PICKS 
PROKOFIEV: Classical Symphony, Op. 25; Ell' 
gene Ormandy conducting the Philadelphia Or 
chestra-Columbia ML 5945 
Prokofiev's forty-seven year old "Classical Sym- 
phony, Op. 25" is given a superb reading by DI' 
gene Ormandy and the Philadelphia Orchestra on 
this new classical offering from Columbia. The 
conductor captures all of the work's buoyant, 
soaring constructions in his straight -forward m 
terpretation. The disk also contains other Pro- 
kofiev selections including his famous "Suite From 
The Love For Three Oranges." A 
standout 
achievement. 
GROFE: Grand Canyon Suite, London Festisal 
Orchestra/Stanley Black-London SPC21002 
London Records debuts its Pop Concert Series or. 
phase 4 with this performance of Ferde Grofe' 
Grand Canyon Suite by the London Festitval Or- 
chestra conducted by Stanley Black. Here's a pat 
standard with classical proportions and this Den 
version is sure to bring the traffic into the shop: 
The stereo is crisp and brilliant and completely 
without gimmickry, and the composer's music 
Is 
as fresh and satisfying as it was when it No' 
first performed three decades ago. Strong chart 
potential here.

"HAPPY END" - Lotte Lenya - Columbia OL 
5630 
Kurt Weill & Bertolt Brecht's "Happy End" per- 
haps had the unhappy fate of following the 
team's "3 Penny Opera," and is today known pri- 
marily as the show that produced two Weill - 
Brecht standbys, "Bilbao Song" and "Surabaya 
Johnny." Weill's widow and superb interpreter 
Lotte Lenya is heard in a brilliantly recorded (in 
Germany) rendition of the "Happy End" score. 
The Weill -Brecht coterie will be dropping in for 
the set, which has an English lyric fly -leaf insert 
for those who don't know German. 
"THE EXCITING SOUND OF ACQUAVIVA"- 
Decca DL4465 
Acquaviva plays pop music with a symphonic 
approach on this new offering from Decca. The 
orkster conducts a big orchestra with plenty of 
lush strings performing thirteen melodic items 
which have been richly orchestrated and inven- 
tively arranged. Programmers and mood music 
buffs will find the entire set a top-notch listening 
experience. Bright bands here are "Green Valley," 
"Dancing Notes," "A New Shade Of Blue" and 
"One Look At You. 
"TOP TV THEMES '64"-Carl Brandt-Warner 
Bros. 1529 
Although all the popular TV programs have 
theme music, because of the dramatic excitement 
of the medium the music is often overlooked. 
Carl Brandt and the Warner Bros. ork takes us 
on a delightful tour of some of this season's most 
well-known tunes on this new disk. The crew 
shines as they render standout renditions of 
"Burke's Law," "Arrest And Trial" and "My 
Favorite Martian." Loads of listening enjoyment 
here. 
"MUSICAL MEMORIES OF LONDON"-Various 
Artists-London International TW 91312 
Jolly old London is delightfully depicted in song 
on this Musical Memories series from London 
International which spotlights the talents of a 
host of British artists. Some of the tunes here 
are known internationally, with the remainder of 
the traditional variety. "A Nightingale Sang In 
Berkely Square," "The Lambeth Walk" and "A 
Foggy Day" are performed by the Mike Sammes 
Singers, Gerry Grant, John Hansen, Vanessa Lee 
and the orks of Ken Jones and J. Gregory. Lots 
of pleasureable listening to be had here. 
"50 FABULOUS LATIN FAVORITES"-Tito 
Rodriguez-United Artists UAL 3345 
Here's another entry from United Artists from 
its "50 Favorite" series, this time spotlighting 
the Latin rhythms of Tito Rodriguez and ork. 
This is a first-rate dance package with plenty to 
offer for the dance buff. The orkster includes 
a large sampling of Cha chas, merengues, mam- 
bos, sambas and guarachas with such tunes as 
"Green Eyes," "Maria Elena," "Cumbanchero" 
and "Lisbon Antigua." Brisk sales are indicated. 
"SWEDISH 
SONGS 
SUNG 
BY 
WILLIAM 
CLAUSON"-MGM E4198 
The folk songs of Evert Taube are performed 
with authority and sensitivity by William Clau- 
son, the Swedish -American folkster, on this new 
offering from MGM. The tenor has a warm and 
expressive voice and delivers these Swedish tunes 
with vigor and polish. The folk purist will find 
much enjoyment in Clauson's handling of "Fra- 
gancia," "Rosa Pa Bal," "Sa Skimrande Var Al- 
drig Havet" and "Balladen Om Gustaf Blom."

"POINT OF DEPARTURE"-Gary McFarland 
Sextet-Impulse A-46 
In an era when vibists are becoming quite rare 
indeed, Gary McFarland comes up with this top- 
drawer set which spotlights his own vibistic 
talents and bows, for the first time on wax, his 
Sextet. The McFarland approach is an easy-going 
midstream style with each member of the group 
given ample opportunity to display his individual 
abilities. Highlights of the disk include "Sand- 
piper," "Hello To The Season" and "I Love To 
Say Her Name." Jazzophiles should find plenty 
to dig here. 
"RIGHT HERE, RIGHT NOW!"-Billy Taylor 
Trio-Capitol T2039 
On rare occasions a jazz artist comes up with 
a pure jazz album with sure-fire best-seller 
potential, and this premier set on Capitol by 
Billy Taylor could be one of them. The deejay 
pianist's flare for melodic jazz coupled with his 
tasteful improvisations make for potent listening 
excitement. A bonus feature here is the big band 
backing of Oliver Nelson which adds the perfect 
touch to the 88'er's handling of "Soul Sister," 
"That's Where It Is" and "I Believe In You." 
Watch it move. 
"SOUL HITS"-Les McCann-Pacific Jazz 78 
Les McCann, who has earned many laurels in the 
past with his personal keyboard jazz styling, 
teams up with an accomplished group of musi- 
cians including Joe Pass (guitar), Paul Cham- 
bers (bass) and Paul Humphrey (drums) on 
this swingin' set which combines the best -ele- 
ments of jazz and blues into one cohesive musical 
expression. Best listening bets here include such 
favorites as "Back At The Chicken Shack," 
"Work Song" and "Groove Yard." 
JAll BEST BETS 
"BLACK MOONLIGHT & SUNSHINE"-Monty 
Sunshine-Kapp KL1356 
Monty Sunshine, who has made quite a name for 
himself in Europe with his distinctive clarinet 
pop -jazz stylings, kicks off his American career 
with this tasteful program of easy-going ever- 
greens. Sunshine and crew effectively couple the 
traditional Dixie sounds with some avant-garde 
doings as they render top-flight readings of "Just 
One More Chance," "That's My Desire" and 
"Charmaine." 
"PAGE ONE"-Joe Henderson-Blue Note 4140 
Joe Henderson makes an impressive 
album 
debut on Blue Note with this pulsating package 
of jazz selections who potently showcases the 
saxaphonist's talent. Backed by Kenny Dorham, 
McCoy Tyner, Butch Warren and Pete LaRoca, 
the saxman takes a very modern but lyrical 
approach to these jazz items and the result is 
outstanding. Jazzophiles will dig his very per- 
sonal 
treatments 
of 
"Homestretch," 
"Blue 
Bossa," "Recordo Me" and "Jinrikisha." A top- 
flight jazz offering.

MOZART: Violin Concertos 4 & 6; Yehudi Menu- 
hin, violinist and the Bath Festival Orchestra- 
Angel S 36152 
Yehudi Menuhin's already impressive reputation 
as an interpreter of the romantic composers is 
further enhanced by this superb Angel offering 
on which the violinist turns in top-flight readings 
of the famous concertos. Menuhin does not resort 
to gimmicks but renders the intricate, complex 
chromatic phrases in a highly-listenable straight- 
forward, lyrical fashion. Classical buyers should 
come out in droves for the package. 
WAGNER: Prelude & Liebestod from Tristan & 
Isolde/Overture & Venusberg Music from Tails 
hauser/Munich Philharmonic, Rudolf Albert. 
Counterpoint 614 
Wagner's immortal Overture from Tannhauser 
and Venusberg Music are executed with artistic 
fervor and sensitivity by the Munich Philhar- 
monic Orchestra under the direction of Rudolf 
Albert, along with the Prelude and Liebento° 
from Tristan and Isolde. The latter opus is the 
perfect fusion of drama and music while the 
Tannhauser depicts a variety of moods and 
emotions. Both works have broad appeal forme 
classical 
devotee. An excellent 
entry 
Everest's classical line.

WP Offers New LP's, 
Pacts 3 Attractions 
In Expansion Moves 
HOLLYWOOD-Along with new al- 
bum product, World Pacific Records 
has announced the inking to exclusive 
contracts of three attractions, one in 
the jazz field, one in bluegrass, the 
other teen -oriented. Move marks the 
label's new expansion drive, which, 
the label expects, will lead to its big- 
gest year. 
Richard Bock, WP head, announced 
that he had signed The Sandells, 
which 
portrays 
the 
"motorcycle 
sound," which Bock says is a follow- 
up to the surfin' and hot -rod ideas. 
The group's first LP is called "The 
Scramblers," from which a single, 
"Out Front," is being issued. 
The jazz inking was Louisiana - 
Texas blues singer Long Gone Miles, 
whose debut on WB will be an album 
in the near future. Long Gone per- 
formed with Lightnin' Hopkins for al- 
most 10 years in Houston before com- 
ing out to the west coast, where for 
the past two years he has been ap- 
pearing in various niteries. On the LP 
date, he's joined by his regular gui- 
tarist, Willy Chambers, and vet jazz 
bassist Leroy Vinnegar. 
Another new act at the label are 
The Kentucky Colonels, a bluegrass 
group. 
The new LP's, on WP's subsid, 
Pacific Jazz, are highlighted by a big - 
band outing (his third for WP) with 
Gerald Wilson called "Musical Por- 
traits." Special promo singles are be- 
ing sent to AM (45) and FM (33) 
outlets. Besides two cuts from the LP, 
the decks also include a rehearsal 
sequence. 
Other new albums, set for Mar. re- 
lease, include "Jazz -Waltz" with Les 
McCann and The Jazz Crusaders, and 
"Flute N' Folk" with Bud Shank and 
The Folkswingers, on WP's subsid 
label, Pacific Jazz. 
Jack Pierce, national sales mana- 
ger, left last week on a sales and 
promo tour to all major markets in 
the east and midwest. 
Lanier Exits Fantasy 
For Indie Promotion 
LOS ANGELES-Warren Lanier has 
announced that he has exited Fan- 
tasy -Galaxy Records where he was a 
sales and promotion representative. 
Lanier advised that he is going into 
independent disk promotion on a local 
and national level, with headquarters 
at 1815 S. Hauser Blvd., L.A. 19, 
Calif. 
Prior to his term with Fantasy - 
Galaxy, Lanier was personal manager 
of Etta Jones for eight years, and 
was a national promo manager for 
Everest Records. 
FCC OK's Sale Of 11 Stations 
In $38 Million Deal 
NEW YORK-The biggest group of 
radio -TV outlets in history-a $38.5 
million package-was approved last 
week by the FCC. In the massive 
transaction, three purchasers will 
take over the 11 radio -TV stations of 
the Transcontinent Television Corpo- 
ration. 
The Taft Broadcasting Company 
paid $26,889,310 for seven stations: 
WGR-AM-FM-TV-Buffalo, 
WNEP- 
TV-Scranton, and 
WDAF-AM-FM- 
TV-Kansas City. Time -Life Broad- 
casting Company paid $1,565,000 for 
KERO-TV-Bakersfield, and Midwest 
Television acquired three stations for 
$10,085,000. The stations are KFMB- 
AM-FM-TV-San Diego. 
The commission vote was 5-1. Com- 
missioner Robert T. Bartley dissented. 
He made 
no statement in voting 
against permitting the transactions. 
20th C -F Expects Profit 
For '63, Music Interests Help 
NEW YORK -20th Century -Fox Pic- 
tures expects to report a profit of 
about $9.1 million for 1963, according 
to Darryl F. Zanuck, president of the 
company. 
At a press conference last week, 
Zanuck noted that the profit-com- 
paring to losses of $39.8 million in 
1962-would not stem from film pro- 
duction 
or distribution, but from 
other operations. With no breakdowns 
available, latter includes 20th Cen- 
tury -Fox Records, music publishing, 
TV, film processing laboratories, oil 
investments and foreign theaters. 
Zanuck, also reporting on the firm's 
go -for -broke flick, "Cleopatra," said 
that the epic had brought $25 million 
into the company and would eventu- 
ally earn $55 million. Sometime ago, 
he predicted a gross of $100,000. 20th 
C -F says the cost of the film was $44 
million. 
Suit Over Vox' "Fidelio" 
Settled Out Of Court 
NEW YORK-An out -of -court settle- 
ment has been reached in a suit by 
the Vienna Philharmonic Orchestra 
and baritone Herbert Alsen against 
Vox Productions, the New York -based 
label. The action was taken against a 
Vox -issued production of "Fidelio," 
which featured the litigants. Under 
the settlement, the set, which Vox re- 
leased initially some years ago, will 
be re -issued with several changes in 
format.

Farewell To The Tumult & Shouting 
NEW YORK-An extremely uninformed passer-by, oblivious to the news of 
the world, would have thought that the above -pictured mobs standing outside 
of New York's Plaza Hotel recently were waiting for a visiting dignitary of 
no less importance than the president of Mars. In reality, the seemingly count- 
less throngs, kept in check by standing and mounted police, were patiently 
waiting for a glimpse of the Beatles. But now it's farewell to all this pan- 
demonium, for last week the group returned home to England.

"I'M GOIN' TO SING SIXTEEN SPIRITUALS" 
-Robert Shaw Chorale-RCA Victor LM 2580 
Robert Shaw directs his musical attention at 
American spirituals on this new Victor offering 
and leads his Chorale in fine program of feeling- 
ful evergreen laments. The big chorus displays an 
amazing understanding of the gospel -folk idiom 
as they render superb versions of "That Lone- 
some Valley," "Steal Away" and "My Soul's Been 
Anchored." 'Deejays should find the material here 
an interesting change of pace. 
"THE BEST OF JESSE CRAWFORD"-Decca 
DXSB 7171 
Jesse Crawford, one of the most consistent best- 
selling organists in the country, demonstrates his 
masterful keyboard technique on two dozen tunes 
that span the musical spectrum on this deluxe 
two -disk set from Decca. The organist plays pop, 
sacred and the classics here on a wide variety of 
melodies that include "Softly, As In A Morning 
Sunrise," "Merry Widow Waltz," "Ave Maria," 
"Wedding March" and many others. Crawford 
fans should come out in force for the set. 
"THIS IS GENE STRIDEL"-Columbia CL 2115 
Gene Stridel makes an impressive wax debut on 
Columbia with this package of ballads and blues 
tunes geared for easy listening. With arrange- 
ments and conducting chores handled by Marty 
Manning, the chanter eases his way through such 
melodic goodies as "After You've Gone," "The 
Sweetest Sounds" and "How Blue The Night." 
The songster has a big emotion -packed voice that 
merits attention from buyers and spinners. 
"MORE OF THE BEST OF JIMMY REED"- 
Vee Jay VJ 1080 
Vet blues songster Jimmy Reed unleashes his po- 
tent, wide -range vocal talents full -blast on this 
top-notch Vee Jay program of blues, evergreens 
and self -penned while -back Reed triumphs. While 
backed by a fine funky combo the chanter -guitar- 
ist really wails on "Baby What's Wrong," "Down 
In Mississippi" and "Caress Me Baby." Disk 
should sell strongly in the r&b markets. 
"SPIKE JONES NEW BAND"-Liberty LRP 
3349 
Spike Jones, who made an abrupt departure from 
his usual musical bill -of -fare with his last Liberty 
LP outing, continues in the same vein with this 
new outing directing his talents to some old and 
new hits. The orkster effectively combines a folk 
flavor with "trad jazz" in an ear -arresting man- 
ner on such oldies as "Kansas City," "Deep Pur- 
ple" and "Charade." Top-notch programming fare. 
"GREAT GOSPEL SONGS"-Tennessee Ernie 
Ford & Jordainaires-Capitol ST 2026 
Tennessee Ernie Ford, with a half dozen best- 
selling religious LP's to his credit, joins the Jor- 
danaires and Boyce Hawkins' gospel piano on 
this package of gospel songs from Capitol. The 
chanter and the quartet effectively combine rev- 
erence with good spirits on these happy tunes as 
they liltingly offer "Hide Me, Rock Of Ages," "A 
Beautiful Life" and "I Can Tell You The Time." 
Brisk sales are indicated. 
"CONCERT AT NEWPORT"-John Lee Hooker 
-Vee Jay VJ 1078 
One of the highpoints of last summer's Newport 
Folk Fest was the appearance of vet blues 
chanter, John Lee Hooker. On this new Vee Jay 
offering, cut live at some of his Newport concerts, 
the artist is presented in a varied program of 
blues laments. While backing himself on the gui- 
tar, Hooker turns in some top-notch performances 
of "I Can't Quit You Now Blues," "Bus Station 
Blues" and "Talk That Talk Baby."

ITALY 
Two events are at the top of this musical week in Italy, and stress out how 
deep is the interest in the music of young people, and of course, also the 
exceptional interest of the music industry in the particular taste of the 
youngsters. 
With the slogan "A New Label for the Young," RCA Italians has an- 
nounced the creation of a new mark completely devoted to the young public. 
The new label is called ARC, but the event is not only limited to the presenta- 
tion of a new series of disks, but shall be considered as the creation of a new 
independent record firm in the bosom of the big RCA Italiana's operation. 
This means that the production of ARC will be handled independently from 
the production of RCA Italiana, and will be promoted and delivered through 
new channels. 
During a cocktail party given in Milan at the presence of all the repre- 
sentatives of the Italian music world, the General Manager of RCA Italiana, 
Giuseppe Ornato introduced the new, young head of the record firm, Sergio 
Bardotti, and the artists who form the first group of new talent under the 
new label. 
The production of the new label will be released through the experienced 
system of indie producers. This system was adopted in Italy for the first 
time by RCA Italiana, followed after by some other record companies. The 
adoption of this new system constituted a revolution on our record -making 
conceptions and it's the first time that a new firm is built exclusively on such 
a format. In fact, until now five producers and talent -scouts have cooperated 
with the debut of the new record company: first on the list is the well known 
indie producer, Nanni Ricordi, who produced the first ARC disk of his new 
singer, Oscar; second is Carlo Rossi, a lyric writer who also makes his debut 
as a record producer, presenting the talent of Roby Ferrante. Third is the 
well known talent -scout Teddy Reno, who produces for ARC. Fourth is an- 
other top lyric writer, Franco Migliacci, who presents his new singer Giancarlo 
Guardabassi, and last but not least is another Migliacci discovery, the young 
artist Gianni Morandi, who reveals his talent as a record producer with the 
first waxing of Ivana Borgia. 
All are extremely young: Roby Ferrante is 19, first record is the San Remo 
hit penned by himself "Ogni Volta." Reno is 18, and his first cut is entitled 
"Eravamo Amici." Ivana Borgia is 16, and her first title recorded is "Fiocca 
Fiocca La Neve." Oscar is 20 and recorded "Vola Con La Spyder" (Italian 
version of "Come On Little Angel"). Giancarlo Guardabassi is 26, the title 
chosen for his debut is "Da Retta A Me." 
The second event of the week concerns EMI Italiana whose idea is con- 
nected with the beginning of a deep revolution in the traditional means for 
record promotion. 
Once again this idea is devoted to young people: It was conceived by the 
young head of the EMI Italiana's press and publicity office, Eraldo Di Vita. 
Under the name Club 45, EMI Italiana has created, in the center of Milan, 
a club for the young. EMI Italiana brings together every Saturday, in a 
big hall, all the members of this new club. There they can dance, listen to 
their favorite singers, speak with them, and what is more interesting, to 
listen and judge the new unpublished disk of the EMI talent. This is the first 
time that such an initiative has taken place in Italy and this creates a direct 
contact and connection between the teeners and the industry which produces 
their favorite entertainment. 
Such a direct contact, as we said above, will create new, important pro- 
motional means that can be considered a new force besides radio, TV and 
the juke box. It's a direct contact between the industry and its potential 
buyers and this direct contact will make it easier to create product according 
to the taste of these young buyers. 
We are sure, of course, that this example will be immediately followed 
by other record companies and this will deeply modify in our country the 
custom of entertainments among the young. 
The first such event conducted by EMI Italiana recently gave unexpected 
results: more than 1,500 young people took part in the first meeting, during 
which EMI Italiana presented the top Belgian/Italian singer Adamo along 
with the upcoming talent of Vasso Ovale, and the new voice of Gianna Foretti. 
The success of the evening was so strong that the police had to calm the big 
enthusiasm of the girls and boys. Adamo, Vasso Ovale, Gianna Foretti pre- 
sented their new recordings, and a strong success in the sales in the shops 
of Milan has served as a confirmation of the strong promotional power of 
such an initiative, which convinced EMI and the organizer Eraldo Di Vita 
at once to open the Club 45 in all the principal centers of Italy. 
Another important event of this week is the visit in Italy of the well known 
jazzman Thelonious Monk of CBS, who gave a concert in Milan on February 
23, and took part also to a TV show with our jazz performers, Basso and 
Valdambrini. Thelonious received a strong welcome: his records, according 
to the sales of jazz disks in Italy, are obtaining a good success on our market 
and his appearance on our TV screen, of course, will increase such sales. 
In this regard we have noted that such personal appearances of such famous 
jazz musicians in our country are strongly contributing to the diffusion of 
jazz in Italy. Other concerts will be given by Monk in Torino and Bologna. 
On the jazz theme, Riccordi has taken the distribution in Italy of the Ameri- 
can catalog Blue Note, formerly distributed by Karim. 
Catherine Spaak, the film actress and songstress, under contract with Dischi 
Ricordi, recorded recently for the background of a new film entitled "I Ma- 
lamondo" two songs, titles of which are "Questi Vent'anni Miei" and "Penso A 
Te." Both songs as well as all the background music of the film are published 
by Campi. The film is a report on European youngsters. 
Tony Dallara, the top artist of the Saar label, has recorded his San Remo hit 
"Come Potrei Dimenticarti" in Japanese. The recording will be distributed in 
Japan by King Records. 
Among the classical releases of the week, let's mention a Decca album 
recorded by Ernest Ansermet. The well known orchestra conductor presents in 
this new album, three of the best pages penned by Ravel Honneger and Dukas: 
First is the "Sorcerer Apprentice" by Dukas, second the "Bolero" and "Valse" 
by Ravel, and third "Pacific 231" by Honegger. 
And we conclude our column mentioning four new groovings of our top 
talent Peppino Di Capri: the four titles chosen by him for his two new singles 
are "Ieri Sera A Quella Festa," "Shout," "Piccatura" and "Chi Accende Le 
Stelle."

The Beatles are coming! That's the word of the day on the German record 
market. The fabulous group from England has cut their first 2 sides in German 
language which will be released on March 6. The tunes are "I Want To Hold 
Your Hand" and "She Loves You" and the two hits are coupled on one single. 
The English versions of the tunes are already racking up tremendous sales and 
a Beatles record should soon find its way into the German top 10. Electrola 
reports that the group is also planning a trip to Germany for p.a.'s and TV 
appearances. In the meanwhile, German A&R men are frantically trying to 
put together groups with the "Liverpool sound" to beat the Beatles to the 
punch. The Searchers have already recorded their hits "Sugar and Spice" and 
"Needles And Pins" in German for Vogue, and another group The Teambeats 
have done "Please Please Me" here. It looks like a good fight is shaping up as 
to who will have the hit group but in any case, the "Liverpool Sound" should 
put a shot in the arm to the sagging singles business in Germany. 3 Beatles 
records are already in Germany's top 50. There's another fight taking place 
in Germany. Tenor Rudolf Schock who is now signed with Ariola's "Eurodisc" 
label has 2 LP's released by his old firm Electrola under the title "Rudolf 
Schock-The Great Years." Eurodisc has tried to put a halt to the sale of the 
two LP's saying that the disks do not represent the artist at his best. A court 
order stop took place but on January 29, the Cologne court of lew decided 
that the records could be released. 
Italian lass Anita Traversi will represent Switzerland at the "Song For 
Europe" contest to be held on March 21 in Copenhagen. The 24 year old 
songstress will do an Italian language tune for the festival. Last year, the 
Swiss entry was Ester Ofarim, who took 2nd place at the festival. Anita 
records for Ariola here. Ariola also reports that Duke Ellington has a tour 
set for Europe from the 2nd of March to the 22nd. He will visit Stuttgart, 
Zurich, Munich, Frankfurt, St. Moritz, Milan, Stockholm, Helsinki, Goteborg, 
Malmo, Copenhagen, Hamburg, Berlin and Paris during the tour. 
Billy Mo from Trinidad was awarded a Tirol Hat for the sale of iz million 
copies of his hit "I'd Rather Buy A Tirol Hat" during the Olympics in Inns- 
bruck. Two other Teldec artists, Vico Torriani and Hannelore Auer, were on 
hand for the award. 
Hans Gerig reports that the firm is swinging with the German version of 
"Sugar And Spice" by The Searchers and two San Remo songs, "Un Bacio 
Piccolissimo" which has been recorded in German by Ulla Niesen for Decca, 
and "Sole Sole" which is the most recorded San Remo tune in Germany, as 
Margot Eskens from Polydor, Siw Malmkvist and Umberto Marcato of Metro- 
nome. Vivi Bach and Dietmar Schoenherr of Philips, Ulla Niesen and Uwe 
Grimm of Decca and Nana Gualdi of Ariola have all done vocal versions of 
the tune in German and Will Glahe is turning out an instrumental version of 
the work. 
CBS publicity man Lothar Graf reports that the firm has signed Olympic 
and world champion skating star Marika Kilius to a contract and her first 
single has already been released. 
Rudy Slezak of Aberbach music tells us that he has a not f"1l of hits at 
present. The Chubby Checker version of "Loddv Lo" is selling like hot cakes 
and the German version of the tune by Gerd Boettcher is doing even better. 
"Bossa Nova Baby" is a top 10 tune with versions by Elvis Presley. Bill Ram- 
sey and Ted Herold racking up top sales. The firm is also moving ont with 
the German version of "A Love So Fine" by Gina Dobra. "The Kind of Bov 
You Can't Forget" by Ingela Brander and the new Presley single "Mexico" 
from his LP "Fun In Acapulco." Teldec Records has a left field hit on their 
hands with a new waxing by newcomer Ronny. It's a German language wax- 
ing of "Oh My Darling Caroline." The record has passed the 50,000 mark in 
2 weeks of sales. Deutsche Grammophon has divided its organization and has 
formed a. "Germany Department" with the pop production of their Polydor 
label falling under this department. The new department goes into effect on 
April 1 and will have offres in Hamburg at. Rothenhaumchaussee 5. The new 
department will handle nll advertising. making of record covers and distribu- 
tion of the Polvdor product. This division will make it possible for more con- 
centrated work on the pop product and the international and classical product.

More Nations Choose Soneis For Eurovision Contest 
ZAGREB, Yugoslavia-Yugoslavia will be represented at the Eurovision Song 
Contest in Copenhagen, March 21, by "Zivot Je Zatvorio Krug" (Life Has 
Closed The Circle), composed by Srdian Matijevic and lyrics by Stevan Raicko- 
vic. It will be sung by Sabahudin Kurt, who is under exclusive contract to 
Jugoton Records in Zagreb. The Yugoslavian delegation will also include an 
orchestra -leader, but the name is not available yet. 
LISBOA, Portugal-"Oraçáo" (Prayer) is title of Portugal's entry at the 
Eurovision Song Festival in Copenhagen in March. It is composed by Joao 
Nobre, lyrics by Rogério Bracinha, and will be sung by Antonio Calvario, 
recording for His Master's Voice in Portugal. The Portuguese delegation to 
Copenhagen will also include orchestra -leader Armando Tavares Belo, who will 
conduct the Portuguese number. The artist, Antonio Calvario, was recently 
voted "King of Portuguese Radio" on a contest held by one of the most im- 
portant local magazines.

"FOREIGN FILM FESTIVAL"-Jo Basile- 
Audio Fidelity AFLP 2124 
Fourteen melody -laden themes from recent flicks 
are surveyed by the orchestra of Jo Basile on this 
album entry from Audio Fidelity. The orkster 
employs a potent rhythm section as the fitting 
complement to the organ, piano and sax solo 
flights. Loads of top listening and dancing enjoy- 
ment to be had here. Rhythmic tracks here are 
"Charade," "Mondo Cane," "Boccaccio 70" and 
"Black Orpheus." 
"DICK SHAWN SINGS WITH HIS LITTLE 
PEOPLE" -20th Century Fox 4124 
Dick Shawn adds another facet to his versatility 
on this program of tunes on which he is joined 
by his Little People. That Shawn is a comic is 
much in evidence here as his approach to these 
tunes is part juvenile, part tongue-in-cheek, but 
wholly entertaining. The comic and the kids are 
obviously enjoying themselves with their treat- 
ments of "La Plume De Ma Tante," "High is 
Better Than Low" and "The Kockamamie." It's a 
delight for kids of all ages-including the elders. 
"SONGS THAT MADE HIM FAMOUS"-Clyde 
Moody-Starday SLP 262 
Clyde Moody's long legions of country fans 
should really dig this Starday album on which 
the vet chanter -guitarist offers a program of his 
previous hits. The songster demonstrates that he 
still has a potent, rich, wide -range baritone voice 
as he renders "Nobody's Business," "Whispering 
Pines" and "What It Means To Be Lonesome." 
Plenty of potential here. 
"HALLELUJAH THE HILLS"-Original Sound- 
track-Fontana MGF 27524 
Adolf Mekas' "Hallelujah The Hills" has been 
hailed as one of the crowning art -film achieve- 
ments of the year. The off -beat, wacky comedy 
was greatly enhanced by an almost as absurd 
score composed by Meyer Kupferman. The music, 
which, for the main, has an interesting semi- 
classical flavor, is divided into various distinctive 
segments each of which underlines a significant 
action in the flick. A thoroughly delightful listen- 
ing experience. 
"DEDICATED TO YOU"-Tommy Dorsey-RCA 
Camden CAS 800 
The Tommy Dorsey band of the thirties and 
forties surveys ten tunes which were typical of 
the times on this issue from Camden. In addition 
to some fine vocals by Frank Sinatra, Jack Leon- 
ard and Edythe Wright, there are some first-rate 
solos by Joe Bushkin, TD, Buddy Rich and Ziggy 
Elman. Lots of nostalgia here with such oldies as 
"Just As Though You Were Here," "Snooty Lit- 
tle Cutie" and "Will You Still Be Mine."

"JAZZ IMPRESSIONS"-Vince Guaraldi-Fan- 
tasy-3359 
Vince Guaraldi made a strong chart showing a 
while back with his "Jazz Impressions Of Black 
Orpheus" set, and could very well repeat that 
success with this first-rate package of jazz items. 
The pianist's highly distinctive style is evident at 
every moment as he serves up captivating rendi- 
tions of some old, some new tunes including "Yes- 
terdays," "Room At The Bottom," "Willow Weep 
For Me" and "Autumn Leaves." Could be an- 
other winner for Guaraldi. 
"PORTRAITS"-Gerald Wilson-Pacific Jazz 80 
The jazz big band era is decidedly over, but Ger- 
ald Wilson and his large crew continue to pro- 
duce exciting, valid musical statements in a large 
group context. The composer -arranger's mid- 
stream orientation is captured on a fine program 
of originals and evergreens including "So What," 
"Ravi" and "'Round Midnight." One of the best 
sets that Wilson has cut in quite a while.

"3 GIANTS"-Sonny Rollins With Clifford Brown 
& Max Roach-Prestige PR 7291 
Although all three of the jazz luminaries here 
have gone their separate ways (Clifford Brown 
died in '56) but their distinctive brand of bebop 
swingin' displayed on this fine Prestige set makes 
for some fine jazz listening. All three men per- 
fectly compliment each other as they blend their 
talents into one cohesive musical unit on "Valse 
Hot," "Kiss And Run" and "I Feel A Song Com- 
ing On." Jazzophiles should dig it. 
"DEBUT IN BLUE"-Gene Shaw-Argo 726 
Gene Shaw, who made his album debut on Argo 
with a set tagged "Breakthrough," follows it with 
this second stanza of jazz tunes delivered in the 
same potent manner. The trumpeter is backed 
throughout by rhythmic section lashing out with 
a heavy beat, some with a strong Latin flavor. 
Jazzophiles will dig these ultra -modern sounds, 
especially the tag tune, "Karachi," "The Gentle 
Princess," "When Sunny Gets Blue" and "Thieves 
Carnival." 
"FIVE ON EIGHT"-Rufus Jones-Cameo 1076 
Rufus Jones bows on Cameo with this package 
of jazz tunes served up in pulsating fashion by 
the drummer and his backdrop combo. The drum- 
mer shines in the solo spotlight along with sax- 
ists Joe Farrell and Seldon Powell on such instru- 
mental goodies as "My Special Dream," "Ebb 
Tide," "A Secret" and "Just About That Time." 
Jazzophiles will dig the set. 
CLASSICAL PICKS 
"OPERATIC RECITAL"-Robert Merrill-Lon- 
don 5833 
The Met's Robert Merrill demonstrates his op- 
eratic versatility on this solo debut on London. 
The baritone delivers arias from seven different 
operas displaying vigor and emotional intensity 
throughout, and his voice is rich with power and 
color. Devotees of Merrill and the opera will 
surely want to hear his interpretations 
of 
"Credo" from Otello, "Il Balen Del Suo Sorriso. 
from Il Trovatore and "Si Puo" from Pagliacci - 
SMETANA: The Bartered Bride: Rudolf KemPe 
conducting the Bamberg Symphony Orchestra- 
Angel 3642 
Bedrich Smetana's one hundred year -old bucolic 
opera is given an impressive reading by Baku 
Kempe conducting the Bamberg SymphonyfOr- 
chestra on this superb classical offering 
Angel. The disk features a host of fine singing 
talent including Pilar Lorengar, Fritz Wunder- 
lich, Gottlob Frick, etc. All of the work's sweep- 
ing, romantic statements are faithfully repro' 
duced on this recording. Classical opera buyeli 
should come out in droves.

SOUND EFFECTS 
DAYTONA SPEEDWAY 
"THESE ARE MY FAVORITE SONGS"-Little 
Willie John-King 895 
Little Willie John is obviously out to please his 
fans with this new King outing. One side of the 
disk contains a tasteful selection of full ork- 
backed slow -moving soulful ballads while the 
other side boasts a top-notch collection of hard - 
driving, uptempo rhythmic blusers. The chanter 
showcases his versatility in either idiom by 
rendering impressive versions of such different 
selections as "Autumn Leaves," "Let Nobody 
Love You," "Inside Information." One of the best 
sets that John has cut in quite a while. 
"THE DO -RE -MI KIDS HOOTENANNY"-Kapp 
KL 1360 
That delightful children's chorus which teamed 
up so successfully with Tom Glazer are back 
again-this time offering a varied pop -folk pro- 
gram of their own. The kids' sparkling, high- 
spirited brand of harmony and rhythmic juxta- 
position are spotlighted on such old favorites as 
"If I Had A Hammer," "Down In The Valley." 
Album looms as a chartsville candidate. 
"FROM SEA TO SKI"-Glaciers-Mercury SR 
60895 
It's getting to be extremely hard to tell where the 
next teen -angled sport -and -music trend will come 
from but if the Glaciers have their way skiing 
will be the "in" activity of the coming months. 
The group's danceable, rhythmic, hot rod -flavored 
sound is effectively showcased on such snowy 
items as "Aspen," "Holiday Inn" and "Slalom." 
An impressive performance. 
"THE NEW SOUND OF FOLK-DIXIE"-Nick 
Dean-Request SRLP 10064 
Nick Dean and the Deans Of Dixieland tastefully 
combine the best in folk and the best in Dixie into 
one cohesive, free -flowing musical matrix on this 
pleasant set from Request. The crew's easy-going 
instrumental style is aptly showcased on "The 
Blue Tail Fly," "Farewell Minka" and "Alouette." 
Delightful listening throughout. 
"SOUND EFFECTS DAYTONA SPEEDWAY" 
-Audio Fidelity DFS 7031 
Sound effects buffs and stereophiles should get 
plenty of high-powered listening from this new 
sound effects offering from 
Audio Fidelity. 
Although there is very little in the way of variety, 
the true sound effects addict will delight in the 
screeching of tires and roaring of engines as the 
racing cars are put through their paces at the 
famed Daytona track. All aspects of the race have 
been included-pit changes, grand stand runs, 
shifting down, etc. 
"BEDTIME STORIES FOR GROWN-UPS"- 
George Jessel-Riot R 304 
The Toastmaster General of the United States 
proves beyond the shadow of a doubt that he is 
still one of the country's top story -tellers. The 
stories here are strictly for grown-ups as the title 
implies, but all are funny and keenly indicative of 
the Jessel sense of humor. His occasional lapses 
into Yiddish to add color to the telling, and his 
many admirers throughout the country will find 
much amusement here. 
"ELOISE BROWN PLAYS HYMNS OF THE 
GOSPEL"-Nashboro LP 7018 
Eloise Brown displays an impressive organ style 
and sincere understanding of the gospel idiom on 
this top-notch disk of sacred songs from Nash - 
boro. The artist does not resort to musical gim- 
micks, but renders each selection a feelingful, 
straight -forward style. Standout tracks here are 
"Highway To Heaven," "Blessed Assurance" and 
"Amazing Grace." Disk should do well in the r&b 
markets.

"TIME CHANGES-Dave Brubeck Quartet- 
Columbia CL 2127 
The Dave Brubeck Quartet comes up with a 
sparkling fifth chapter in its "Time ..." series on 
this Columbia jazz outing. The best-selling 
pianist -composer scored chart successes with two 
earlier issues, "Time Out" and "Time Further 
Out," and makes a strong bid for the same sales 
success with this one. The jazz here is high -style, 
modern and potent throughout. Jazzophiles will 
dig Brubeck's handling of "Iberia," "Unisphere" 
and the haunting "Elementals." 
"3 IN JAZZ"-Gary Burton, Sonny Rollins & 
Clark Terry-RCA Victor LPM 2725 
Here's an interesting jazz offering which should 
appeal to a wide variety of fans. Set boasts the 
distinctive vastly different talents of three well- 
known jazzmen: Gary Burton (for those who like 
modern swingin' jazz), Sonny Rollins (for those 
who dig their sounds à la improvisation) and 
Clark Terry (for those with nostalgic ears for 
the old big band swing era). Deejays will find 
plenty of spinnable material here. 
"THE FREEDOM RIDER"-Art Blakey & Jazz 
Messengers-Blue Note 4156 
Art Blakey, who has earned many laurels in the 
past with his distinctive brand of jazz drumming, 
unleashes his potent instrumental talents full - 
blast on this high-powered set from Blue Note. 
All the emotional stops have been pulled out as 
Art and the Messengers go through their paces in 
a relaxed style of improvisation. Highlights of 
the disk are "Tell It Like It Is," "The Freedom 
Rider" and "Blue Lace." 
"COLTRANE 
LIVE 
AT 
BIRDLAND"-John 
Coltrane-Impulse A-50 
The vet saxist (he plays both tenor and soprano 
on this set) teams up with an accomplished crew 
of jazzmen including McCoy Tyner, Jimmy Gar- 
rison and Elvin Jones on this hard-swingin mid- 
stream session from Impulse. While effectively 
backed by the boys, Coltrane's rhythmic, funky 
style of highly -personal wailing is spotlighted on 
"Afro -Blue," "I Want To Talk" and "Your Lady." 
Jazzophiles should come out in droves for the set.

"SOMETHING'S HAPPENING"-Paul Bryant- 
Fantasy 3357 
Paul Bryant adds new dimensions to the organ 
as a jazz instrument on this album romp from 
Fantasy. The organist gets some swinging assist- 
ance from a combo that spotlights the talents of 
saxist Jules Broussard, drummer Johnny Kirk- 
wood and tenor saxman Plas Johnson, all of 
whom perfectly complement the talents of the 
keyboard artist. Bright bands here are "Flutter," 
"Bye Bye Blackbird" and "Why Me?" Loads of 
good listening to be had here. 
CLASSICAL PICKS 
BEETHOVEN: Sonata No. 8; DEBUSSY: Three 
Preludes; Chopin: Etude in C Minor-Vladimir 
Horowitz, pianist-Columbia ML 5941 
Vladimir Horowitz offers an interesting, musi- 
cally varied program of poular selections from 
Beethoven, Debussy and Chopin on this new 
classical offering from Columbia. Part of the 
pianist's amazing skill is his versatility which 
lets him read the intricate Beethoven passages 
with the same verve and assurance as he delivers 
some of the lush, melodic sections of Debussy. 
Classical buyers come out in force for the 
package. 
"EL AMOR BRUJO/LES NUITS D'ETE"-Leon-

Manuel de Falla's vocal -orchestral suite and 
Berlioz' Nuits d'Ete are performed by 
Met 
soprano Leontyne Price and the Chicago Sym- 
phony Orchestra under the baton of Fritz Reiner 
on this new classical entry from RCA Victor. The 
Berlioz opus is ripely melodic and the Falla suite 
is characterized by ringing songs, both of which 
get the full dramatic impact of the soprano s 
range and interpretive talent. The disk is a superb 
classical offering.
