Bill Wagner Joins 
Capitol In New Post 
HOLLYWOOD-Bill 
Wagner 
has 
joined Capitol Records in a new post, 
coordinator of A&R services, accord- 
ing to A&R vp Voyle Gilmore. 
Wagner, reporting directly to Karl 
Engemann, A&R director, will work 
closely with Gilmore and Engemann 
in providing liaison between the la- 
bel's A&R operation and the sales 
and merchandising departments of 
Capitol Records Distributing Corp. 
(CRDC). 
While not previously a member of 
the Capitol staff, Wagner has had 
close dealings with the label since 
1957, when he came to Hollywood as 
the personal manager of The Four 
Freshmen, longtime Capitol act whose 
association with Wagner ended last 
June. 
Before guiding the career of the 
songsters, he was an arranger -con- 
ductor and worked in several groups 
as a jazz trumpet player. As a World 
War 2 pilot, he received the Air Med- 
al and Distinguished Flying Cross. 
Millie Small LP Rushed, 
Re -Package Miller Set 
NEW YORK-Millie Small, hitting 
big with her disking of "My Boy Lol- 
lipop," has made it into the LP field 
in the U.S. with a rush -release from 
Smash Records. 
Titled "My Boy Lollipop-Millie 
Small," the album features all selec- 
tions in a Blue Beat-Ska rhythm. 
The LP, according to Charlie Fach, 
label topper, will be the source of 
the English performer's next singles 
release. She's set for her first U.S. 
visit beginning July 27, when a press 
reception will be held in New York. 
Her manager -guardian, Chris Black- 
well, will accompany her. 
Reacting to another singles hit, the 
label has re -packaged a Roger Miller 
album to take advantage of his strong 
chart stand, "Dang Me." Set is now 
called "Roger Miller-Dang Me." 
3rd Son For Howards 
NEW YORK-Ira Howard, Cash Box 
editor, became the father of his third 
son when his wife, Beverly, gave 
birth last week (7) at Leroy Hospital, 
this city. The boy weighing -in at 
7 lbs., 1 oz., was named Corey Lee. 
The Howards' other children are 
Jamie, 3, and Kevin, 2. The Howard 
family is rounded out by a poodle, 
Happy, aged 1. 
Marvin Cane's 
Wife Dies 
NEW YORK-Elayne Cane, wife of 
Marvin Cane, vp of Screen Gems - 
Columbia Music, died here last week 
(5) in Mount Sinai Hospital after a 
long illness. She was 38 -years old. 
Besides her husband, she is survived 
by three children, Michael 4, Barbara, 
11, Joy, 14, her mother and two 
brothers.

MUSIC FOR WRAT FINK LOVERS 
THE FIRST 12 SIDES OF JUST IV-Liberty 
LRP 3340 
If this initial pop -folk offering from Liberty is 
any indication of their talents, the Just IV have 
a promising future indeed. The crew displays a 
remarkable freshness of style and a distinctive 
full-bodied gusto on the entire gamut of folk 
expression. Best listening tracks here include 
"Gonna Be Singin' In That Land," "San Fran- 
cisco Bay Blues" and "The Universal Soldier." A 
group to watch. 
NEW TOP HITS IN THE GLENN MILLER 
STYLE-Tex Beneke, Ray Eberle, Modernaires 
-Capitol ST 2093 
Tex Beneke, Ray Eberle and the Modernaires 
offer proof positive that the Glenn Miller style of 
playing is never out of fashion, that it remains 
constant through all the musical fads. The band, 
soloists and vocalists combine nostalgia with pres- 
ent day melody on this program of current hits 
on Capitol. "Wives And Lovers," "Bluesette," 
"Java" and "Stay With Me" are just a few of the 
very danceable-listenable tunes included here. 
MEET GINNY ARNELL-MGM E 4228 
Ginny Arnell makes her album debut on MGM 
with this set of teen -angled items that serve as a 
top-drawer showcase for her winning vocal style. 
The lark includes her first single hit, "Dumb - 
head," and the click follow-up entries, "I Wish 
I Knew What Dress To Wear" and "Let Me Make 
You Smile Again" along with nine other simi- 
larly -oriented tunes. The thrush's past single 
sales record could spark some interest for this 
premier LP effort. 
BEST OF THE BLUES-Volume 2-Various 
Artists-Imperial LP 9259 
The label created plenty of interest with their 
initial blues set and this generous second helping 
spotlighting 
such stellar artists as Lightin' 
Hopkins, Floyd Dixon, Peppermint Harris, Amos 
Milburn and Fats Domino gives every indication 
of reaping plenty of loot. Among the standout 
tracks here are "Every Night" by Fats Domino 
and "Feel So Bad" by Lightnin' Hopkins. Album 
is a natural for heavy r&b airplay. 
WILD ORCHIDS-Rex Kona-Columbia CL 2174 
Rex Kona and his Mandarins effectively and 
happily combine Eastern and Western instrumen- 
tation on this program of American and Oriental - 
flavored tunes on Columbia. Although the album 
is mostly pop, there is a trace of jazz in some of 
the arrangements to set the proper mood. Loads 
of delightful listening to be had here as the 
crew surveys such melodic gems as "Kisses 
Sweeter Than Wine," "Moonlight In Vermont," 
"Ginza Girl" and "Patricia." 
ORGAN & PIANO MUSIC-Various Artists- 
MGM 2E-8 
Ferrante & Teicher, Roger Williams, Richard 
Ellsasser and the Manhattan Piano Quartet are 
featured on this 2 -pocket set from MGM (2 for 
the price of 1 Limited Edition series). In a wide 
variety of musical offerings, the pianists and 
organist include "Waltz From Serenade For 
Strings," "The Very Thought Of You," "Love 
Walked In" and "The Lord's Prayer." The listen- 
ing enjoyment is first-rate throughout and the 
set merits special attention. 
JACKIE KANNON'S MUSIC FOR RAT FINK 
LOVERS-Rat Fink 1313 
Ten of the most tuneful and most popular 
tunes of all time are performed by a lush ork 
and sans -lyric chorus on this album deceptively 
tagged, "Music For Rat Fink Lovers"-and 
sports the kookiest set of liner notes any album 
ever had. The music is not all there is to this 
set. Each lush instrumental is followed by a bit 
of surprising commentary. This is mood listening 
at its most unusual. Some of the tunes are 
"Young At Heart," "Small World," "Days Of 
Wine & Roses" and "This Love Of Mine." 
meedes 
slaw prays lME 
HAVIN' A BALL AT THE VILLAGE GATE- 
Lambert, Hendricks & Bavan-RCA Victor LSP 
2891 
Here is a "live" session by Lambert, Hendricks 
& Bavan cut during a recent stint at Gotham's 
Village Gate. The mood on this set is strictly good 
fun and the jazz vocalists go all out for a good 
time here as they romp through "Jumpin' At The 
Woodside," "Days Of Wine & Roses," "With 'Er 
Ead Tucked Underneath 'Er Arm," "Stops And 
Goes Blues" and other rollickers. The trio has a 
large following and this addition to their catalog 
should be much appreciated. 
STITT PLAYS BIRD-Sonny Stitt-Atlantic 1418 
Although Sonny Stitt, like most jazzman who 
broke in prior to World War II has been strongly 
influenced by Charlie Parker, he has developed an 
approach completely his own. On this new At- 
lantic outing the alto saxist plays a musical 
tribute to his mentor by offering a fine sampling 
of Parke -associated tunes. While backed by a 
small swingin' combo Stitt turns in first-rate 
renditions of "Au Privave," "Parker's Mood" and 
"Ko-Ko."

FLUTE FEVER-Jeremy Steig Quarter-Colum- 
bia CL 2136 
Once in a great while a new jazz talent of 
special merits comes on the scene. Such a talent is 
Jeremy Steig. This youthful flutist, featured here 
on his premiere LP, displays a rich full-bodied yet 
lyrical approach to a fine collection of originals 
and sturdies. Although this is Steig's show credit 
must be given to Denny Zeitlin who demonstrates 
a fine piano technique. Jazzophiles should really 
dig the set. 
GOOD GRACIOUS!-Lou Donaldson-Blue Note 
4125 
Vet jazz alto saxist Lou Donaldson really cooks 
up a storm on this swingin' Blue Note session of 
recent vintage oft -requested favorites. Donaldson 
does not carbon -copy other midstream horn men 
but constructs some extremely distinctive, highly - 
personal valid statements. Best bets here include 
"Bad John," "The Holy Ghost" and "Don't'Worry 
'Bout Me." 
TWO JIMS AND ZOOT-Jimmy Raney, Jim Hall, 
Zoot Sims-Mainstream 6013 
The jazz buffs who've enjoyed the guitar play- 
ing of Jimmy Raney and Jim Hall will certainly 
dig this teaming up of the two instrumentalists. 
Also in the solo spotlight is Zoot Sims on tenor 
sax, with all three ably backed by Steve Swallow 
on bass and Osie Johnson on drums. The guitar 
solos are both inventive and tasteful, and Sims 
sax work is warm all the way. Bright bands here 
are "A Primera Vez," "Este Seu Olhar" and 
"Move It." 
CLASSICAL PICKS 
Cecil 
ùineer 
Symphony Nol 
IMBRIE: Violin Concerto, EFFINGER: Little 
Symphony No. 1-Columbia Symphony Orch., 
Carroll Glenn-Columbia MS 6597 
Zoltan Rozsnyai conducts the Columbia Sym- 
phony Orchestra with Carroll Glenn as violinist 
on this first recorded performance of two major 
modern compositions: Imbrie's Concerto for Violin 
& Orchestra and Cecil Effinger's Little Symphony 
No. 1. Both works won for their composers the 
coveted Naumberg Award. They are excitingly 
and sensitively executed here on Columbia. The 
serious student will welcome this modern classical 
disk. 
RODRIGO: Concierto de Aranjuez for Guitar and 
Orchestra; Julian Bream, guitarist; Colin Davis 
conducting the Melos Chamber Orchestra-RCA 
Victor LM 2730 
Julian Bream displays a remarkable sensitivity 
and virtuosity on the classical guitar on this 
excellent album highlighting Rodrigo's "Concierto 
De Arnajuez" and featuring Colin Davis conduct- 
ing the Melos Chamber Orchestra. The artist 
bravely explores all the various tonal qualities of 
his instrument as he reads the work with a 
dazzling sense of purpose. The disk also includes 
selections from Britten and Vivaldi. A superior 
classical offering.

THANKS FOR NOTHING-Rosemary Clooney- 
Reprise RS 6108 
Rosemary Clooney displays the bluesy side of 
her vocal coin on this excellent set of sturdies 
from Reprise. The songstress does not carbon - 
copy anybody but goes through her paces in her 
highly -personal low-key, sensual style. Among 
the highlights of the disk are "Hello Faithless," 
"Just One Of Those Things" and "The Man That 
Got Away." Deejays should find loads of program- 
mable material here. 
SLIPPIN' AROUND-George Morgan & Marion 
Worth-Columbia CL 2197 
George Morgan and Marion Worth tag this 
new Columbia set after their recent country hit 
of "Slippin' Around" and include eleven other 
romantic c&w items. The artists successfully 
blend their distinctive vocal talents into one 
cohesive musical unit as they render "Please Help 
Me I'm Falling," "Sin And Silver" and "The Eyes 
Of The World." Album should sell nicely in the 
country markets. 
JENNIE-Jennie Smith-Dot 25586 
Jennie Smith pays a musical tribute to her 
"discoverer," Steve Allen, by offering an entire 
program of selections composed by the multi- 
talented laughman on this new Dot offering. The 
lark's rich wide -range vibrant voice and lyrical 
distinctive delivery carries her in good stead on 
"Spring In Maine," "I Love You Today" and "The 
Things My Heart Tells Me." One of the best 
albums that the artist has cut in quite a while. 
BEER + PRETZELS + MUSIC = FUN-Matys 
Bros.-Select SL 1108 
The Matys Bros., who came up with a sleeper 
hit about ea year ago tagged, `Who Stole The 
Keeshka," continue in the same vein with this 
Select package of happy -sounding tunes geared 
for listening and dancing fun. Most of the tunes 
here are from the archives (Beer Barrel Polka, 
Pennsylvania Polka etc.) and some are lesser 
known (Cut The Meat Balls In Half, Ain't That 
New York City Somethin') but just as contagious. 
The lads have enlisted a large following that'll 
dig this album effort. 
THE IMPORTANCE OF BEING OSCAR (Part 
II)-Michael MacLiammoir-Columbia OS 2490 
Columbia Records adds to its growing catalog 
of dramatic spoken word offerings with this Part 
II edition of "The Importance Of Being Oscar" 
with Michael MacLiammoir and directed by Hilton 
Edwards. Excerpts from Wilde's "De Profundis," 
"The Ballad of Reading Gaol," and from his 
prison conversations with the warden are included 
here. The 1961 Dublin -Gate Theater Production 
was much heralded by press and public, and this 
recorded version merits a special place on the 
cast shelf. 
GO APE WITH THE KNOCKOUTS-Tribute LP 
1202 
The Knockouts lash out with some of the 
wildest rhythms and sounds ever put on record on 
this Tribute Records album debut. This is rock 
and roll, rhythm and blues, comedy and gospel all 
rolled into one. The group is at times unbelievable, 
but it covers a wide musical spectrum here with 
"Mo Jo Part I" (a while -back click single), 
"Ecuador," "Poor Boy-Rich Boy" and many 
others. The teen dance set will go for this one. 
WE'VE GOTTA SING-Couriers-Warner Bros. 
1547 
The Couriers are back again with another 
generous portion of their easy-going brand of 
gospel singing on this new Warner Bros. entry. 
Although the quintet's repertoire consists mostly 
of traditional items, their approach is modern and 
appealing. Highlights here include "Marching To 
Zion," "I Know He Cares" and "Let Us Walk, 
Walk And Talk."

PRAYER MEETIN'-Jimmy Smith-Blue Note 
4164 
Jimmy Smith, whose accomplishments on the 
organ are now legend, unleashes his potent mid- 
stream jazz talents full -blast on this high-powered 
set cut during his days with the Blue Note label. 
In addition to the organist, the session spotlights 
the funky tenor sax artistry of Stanley Turren - 
tine. Best listening bets include "Prayer Meetin'," 
"Stone Cold Dead In The Market" and "When The 
Saints Go Marching In." Jazzophiles should really 
dig it. 
VIBRATIONS-Milt Jackson-Atlantic 1417 
Vet jazz vibraharpist Milt Jackson teams up 
with an accomplished crew of jazzmen on this 
bright Atlantic set including Tommy Flanagan 
(piano), Kenny Burrell (guitar), George Duviver 
(bass) and Connie Kay (drums.) However, the 
solo spotlight is fixed firmly on Jackson as he 
goes through his melodic low-key paces with verve 
and feeling. Real cookin' tracks here are "Algo 
Bueno," "Blue Jubilee" añd "Let Me Hear The 
Blues." 
JAll BEST BETS 
TRIO 64-Bill Evans-Verve V8578 
Bill Evans comes up with a bag of standards 
for this new jazz outing on Verve, a program 
geared to surprise as well as delight his follow- 
ing. The pianist plays the improbable here, in his 
distinctively personal way, with such unorthodox 
jazz tunes as "Santa Claus Is Coming To Town" 
and "Little Lulu." For a well-balanced repertoire, 
the 88'er includes feelingful renditions of "A 
Sleeping Bee" and "Dancing In The Dark." Evans 
is supported by basist Gary Peacock and drummer 
Paul Motian. 
CHET BAKER SINGS-World Pacific 1826 
That singin' jazzman, Chet Baker, is back again 
in a sparkling World -Pacific set of evergreen 
vintage material. Baker, who plays a first-rate 
midstream trumpet, displays an easy-going, la- 
conic voice and a commanding sense of phrasing. 
While accompanying himself and backed by a 
small jazz combo, he offers top-flight renditions 
of "My Funny Valentine," "That Old Feeling" and 
"But Not For Me." Disk should attract both jazz 
and pop fans. 
SOUL SHOUTIN'-Shirley Scott, Stanley Tur- 
rentine-Prestige PR7312 
Shirley Scott teams up with hubby Stanley 
Turrentine for this rockin' jazz romp on Prestige. 
The electric organ and the tenor sax are delight- 
fully and pulsatingly 'wedded on this first-rate 
session appropriately tagged "Soul Shoutin'." 
Both artists shine in the solo spotlight and per- 
fectly complement each other. For those who like 
their jazz with a driving beat and comprehensible 
melody, Scott and Turrentine offer 
` Serenata,' 
"Gravy Waltz" and others. 
CLASSICAL PICKS 
BEETHOVEN: Violin Concerto in D; 
Joseph 
Szigeti, violinist; Antal Dorati conducting the 
London Symphony Orchestra-Mercury SR90358 
Joseph Szigeti interprets Beethoven's "Violin 
Concerto" with such a completely firm attack that 
it 
should please 
even the 
most 
discerning 
classical buyers. Szigeti highlights all of the in- 
tricate tonal values of the work while not neglect- 
ing the chromatic figurations. In addition to the 
violinist's masterful performance, Antàl Dorati 
shines, as always, in his conducting of the London 
Symphony. A superior classical offering. 
PIANO PIECES FOR CHILDREN-Andre Previn 
-Columbia ML5986 
Andre Previn is a pianist and composer whose 
talents run the gamut of musical expression. On 
this new album from Columbia, the pianist directs 
his attention to a series of classical melodies from 
the pens of Mozart, Mendelssohn, Musorgsky and 
the label's prexy, Goddard Lieberson, all of them 
aimed at the musical appreciation of the younger 
set. Good adult listening too as Previn essays 
Variations on Ah! Vous Dirai -Je, Maman, Six 
Children's Pieces and A Child's Joke and Inter- 
mezzo.

Distrib-Factory Phono 
Sales Down From Jan. -May, 
Distrib Radio Sales Up 
WASHINGTON, D.C.-Distrib and 
factory sales of all kinds of phonos 
were down for the first five months 
of 1964, while distrib radio sales were 
up, according to the Electronic In- 
dustries Association (EIA). 
Jan. -May distrib totals of portable/ 
table model phono sales were 771,839, 
compared to 907,689 in the same 
period of 1963. Distrib sales of con- 
soles were 532,309, compared to 536,- 
738 in the first four months of 1963. 
Factory 
sales 
of portable/table 
model phonos were 736,448 for the 
first four months of this year, while 
last year's total came to 885,380. 
Factory sales of consoles reached 
503,792 in 1964, and 553,719 for 1963. 
Distrib sales of radios were 3,151,- 
201 compared to 3,123,747 units for 
the first five months of 1963. The 
production of radio receivers totaled 
7,168,354 units, compared to 6,931,- 
372 in 1963. A total of 3,417,048 auto 
sets were produced in the first five 
months of 1963, compared to 3,082,- 
520 units in the same period of 1963. 
Together Wherever 
They Sing Folk 
NEW YORK-Elektra folk artists 
Judy Collins and Theodore Bikel will 
make the folk concert scene together 
in Denver, Hollywood and Newport 
during July. On the 17th it was the 
Hollywood Bowl, the 18th at the Red 
Rock Music Festival near Denver and 
the 25th at the Newport Jazz Festival 
in Rhode Island. Judy Collins has 
three LP's in the Elektra catalog, 
with another due in the fall, which 
will contain her Mar. 1964 Town Hall 
appearance, and will go under the 
title of "The Judy Collins Concert." 
Bikel, a longtime Elektra pactee, has 
cut 16 albums for the label. 
Capitol Names 
Engineering Director 
HOLLYWOOD-Capitol Records has 
named Carl S. Nelson, Jr. to the post 
of director of electrical engineering, 
it was announced last week by Ed 
Uecke, administrator of recording 
operations. 
He'll be responsible for the admin- 
istration and supervision of the elec- 
tronic engineering laboratory and 
electronic development engineering. 
Before coming to Capitol, Nelson 
helped to re -design and develop the 
Westrex 
Stereo disk 
system. 
He 
worked on the Todd-Ao Sound System 
from July, 1953 to July, 1955. He also 
was affiliated with Rytron, Inc. and 
Litton Data Systems, transferring to 
Litton's Westrex division last year.

WP's Bock, Pearce 
Start 3 -Week Promo Trek 
HOLLYWOOD-Richard Bock, head 
of the World Pacific and Pacific Jazz 
labels, starts a national promo tour 
this week (20) throughout the east, 
south and midwest. Accompanied by 
Jack Pearce, sales topper, he'll visit 
New York, Chicago, Cleveland, Phila- 
delphia, Baltimore, Nashville, Atlanta 
and other cities. Starting in New 
York, the execs will spend three weeks 
contacting distribs and deejays. While 
in Gotham, Bock will record jazz 
pianist Les McCann for Pacific Jazz 
at Birdland. 
Specific product they will plug will 
include a single, "If You Want This 
Love" by Sonny Knight on Aura, a 
WP album, "Big Ball in Monterey," 
by 
the Stoneman 
Family, 
who've 
made TV appearances on the Steve 
Allen and Meredith Willson TV'ers. 
Group also has a single from the LP, 
"Take Me Home" and "Ground Hog." 
Another date that interests the pair 
is 13 -year -old Jessie Paul's "Corners 
of the Room," produced by Hollywood 
indie producer Jimmy King for World 
Pacific.

######## cb 1964-08-01 p20  [blue\s+note]
Set Re -Issue Of 
Kempff's Complete 
Beethoven Sonatas 
NEW YORK-In honor of pianist 
Wilhelm Kempff's first U.S. recital, 
MGM 
Records has arranged with 
Deutsche Grammophon, whose records 
it distributes in this country, to re- 
issue in Oct. Kempff's vaunted re- 
cordings of the Beethoven Piano So- 
natas. The Complete Beethoven Piano 
Sonatas will comprise ten disks as a 
boxed set (not available singly) to be 
released shortly before the pianist 
gives his American deput recitals at 
New York's Carnegie Hall on Oct. 13 
and 15. 
Each of the ten records has been 
re -mastered and newly pressed. The 
sonatas in Kempff's versions origin- 
ally were released on American press- 
ings starting in 1952 and totaled 15 
records, compared to 10 in this new 
edition and to 13 in the recently re- 
issued Schnabel set on Angel. 
Also in Oct., MGM will release four 
new DGG albums by Kempff, two de- 
voted to Brahms' piano music (the 
intermezzi, rhapsodies and capriccios 
of Opp. 76, 79, 116, 117, 118, 119) and 
two new recordings of the last four 
Beethoven piano sonatas, which will 
comprise one of the pianist's Carnegie 
Hall Programs. 
Kempff's presently available DGG 
recordings include the five Beethoven 
piano concertos, two albums of Mo- 
zart piano concertos (Nos. 8, 23, 24, 
27), an album of Mozart sonatas and 
fantasias and a single disc of the 
Beethoven "Moonlight," "Pathetique" 
and "Appassionata" piano sonatas. 
Kempff, who has appeared in Cana- 
da but never before in the U.S., was 
born in Juterborg on Nov. 25, 1895. 
His father was a piano teacher. 
Kempff, who was well known at the 
age of 20, succeeded Max Pauer as 
director of the Wurttemberg Academy 
of Music (Stuttgart) in 1924 but 
resigned in 1929 to devote himself to 
the piano and to his master classes.

World Artists Bows 
American Arts Subsid 
PITTSBURGH-Lou Guarino, presi- 
dent of World Artists Records, has 
announced the formation of a new 
subsid label to be called American 
Arts. 
Already patted to the new label are

Guarino also announced the distribu- 
tion set-up for the affiliate would be 
the same as for World Artists.

POP BEST BETS 
HI -HEEL SNEAKERS-Tommy Tucker-Check- 
er 2990 
Tommy Tucker tags this new Checker LP offer- 
ing after his recent giant pop-r&b triumph of 
"Hi -Heel Sneakers" and includes eleven other po- 
tent blues items of both the uptempo and ballad 
variety. While backed by a fine funky combo the 
songster dishes -up soulful renditions of "Long 
Tall Shorty," "It's A Mighty Hard Way" and 
"Just For A Day." Plenty of sales potential here. 
MUSIC FROM THE NIGHT OF THE IGUANA 
-Benjamin Frankel-MGM E 4247 
Benjamin Frankel has created a moving, vi- 
brant score for the soon -to -be -released Richard 
Burton -Ava Gardner starrer, "The Night Of The 
Iguana." The music, which utilizes various dif- 
ferent components including classical, jazz and 
Mexican strains, powerfully underlines the dra- 
matic qualities of Tennessee Williams' bold story. 
Disk also inclues some south-of-the-border.selec- 
tions not on the soundtrack. LP should do well 
when the film goes into general release. 
THE LAST TIME I SAW PARIS-Jane Morgan 
-Colpix CP 469 
Jane Morgan pays a melodic homage to the city 
of light with this new Colpix outing that happily 
combines the warm Morgan voice with just the 
right amount of Gallic charm to insure authen- 
ticity. The lark gets things going with Aznavour's 
poignant "The Time Is Now" and follows it with 
haunting renditions of "Autumn Leaves," "If You 
Love Me" and many others. Gliding easily from 
English into French, the thrush is sure to get 
plenty of deejay attention with this effort. 
THE MOON-SPINNERS-Original Soundtrack- 
Buena Vista BY 3323 
The music from Walt Disney's new suspense 
thriller is highlighted on this soundtrack offering. 
from Buena Vista. With a score composed and 
conducted by Ron Grainer and the "Moon -Spin- 
ners Song" by Terry Gilkyson, the music holds 
up well out of context and should get plenty of 
attention with the current release of the flick. The 
flavor is liltingly Mediterranean. Pleasant listen- 
ing throughout, particularly the main theme. 
BY REQUEST-Ferlin Husky-Capitol ST 2101 
One of the best indications a performer has in 
regard to the success of a particular song is how 
it goes over with the "folks out front."Ace coun- 
try chanter Ferlin Husky utilizes this adage with 
this top -rung set of oft -requested tunes from his 
recent p.a.'s and club dates. The songster's rich 
wide -range voice carries him in fine stead on 
"Timber, I'm Falling," "The Face Of A Clown" 
and "Love Looks Good On You." 
THE UNIQUE ARTISTRY OF PEGGY STUART 
COOLIDGE-London PS 377 
Peggy Stuart Coolidge makes an impressive 
disk debut on London Records with this collection 
of standards and originals. The pianist -composer - 
conductor displays a delicate but firm touch as 
she artistically surveys "Yesterdays," "Someone 
To Watch Over Me," a bolero -fashioned reading 
of "Laura," and her own compositions "Smoky 
Eyes" and "Melody Out Of The Night." A mood 
package that merits the attention of spinners and 
buyers everywhere. 
COME RAIN, COME SHINE - Vivienne Della 
Chiesa -20th Century Fox TFM 3140 
Vivienne Della Chiesa, equally at home on the 
stage of an opera house or a nitery floor, makes 
an impressive album debut on 20th Century Fox 
with this collection of ear -pleasing evergreens. 
Harold Arlen, Ellington, Mercer and Lerner & 
Loewe have provided a top-drawer showcase for 
the lark's winning vocal charms as she feeling - 
fully reads "Come Rain Or'Come Shine," "On The 
Street Where You Live" and "Don't Worry 'Bout 
Me." The chanteuse's loyal coterie of admirers 
will enjoy the set.

THE DOUBLE SIX OF PARIS SING RAY 
CHARLES-Philips 600-141 
The Double Six of Paris, who have been ex- 
tremely successful with their previous two al- 
bums, offer an excellent musical tribute to Ray 
Charles on this swingin' set of tunes firmly -asso- 
ciated with The Genius. The group's distinctive 
brand of jazz scat -singing and counterpoint seems 
aptly suited to such Charles "gems" and "One 
Mint Julep," "Let The Good Times Roll By" and 
"Hit The Road Jack." Disk should skyrocket. 
THE OSCAR PETERSON TRIO PLAYS-Verve 
8591 
Oscar Peterson, aided by bassist Ray Brown 
and drummer Ed Thigpen, demonstrates the key- 
board style that has made him one of the most 
"listenable" jazz pianists on the scene today as 
he romps and glides feelingfully through such me- 
lodic gems as "Satin Doll," "This Nearly Was 
Mine," "Fly Me To The Moon," "Shiny Stockings" 
and others. The 88'er is in top form here and the 
package has more than just jazz appeal. 
RUSSIA GOES JAZZ - Various Artists - UAS 
6365 
Teddy Charles and the All -Stars come up with 
some interesting and inventive treatments of 
eight traditional and modern Russian melodies. 
Launching the set with "Scheherazade Blue," the 
crew continues with vibrant readings of "Love 
For Three Oranges," "Dance Arabe," and a pul- 
sating "Borodin Bossa Nova." The aggregation in- 
cludes Jimmy Giuffre, Osie Johnson, Zoot Sims, 
Jimmy Raneys and others equally important. 
Very flavorful jazz session. 
JAll BEST BETS 
PERCEPTION-The Art Farmer Quartet-Argo 
738 Art Farmer directs his considerable talent to 
the fluegelhorn for this new jazz outing on Argo. 
Harold Mabern on piano, Tommy Williams on 
bass, and Roy McCurdy on drums complete the 
crew and lend well -coordinated assistance to the 
leader's efforts. Farmer's slick handling of a mel- 
ody is much in evidence here, particularly on the 
Rodgers and Hart oldies, "Blue Room" and "No- 
body's Heart." A first-rate jazz offering. 
PEOPLE-Roy Haynes-Pacific Jazz 82 
Vet jazz drummer Roy Haynes teams -up with 
an accomplished crew of musicians including 
Frank Strozier (alto & flute), Sam Dockery (pi- 
ano) and Larry Ridley (bass) on this blue-ribbon 
set of chestnuts from Pacific. Although everyone 
gets a chance to show his stuff, the show is really 
all the drummer's as he shines on potent mid- 
stream readings of "The Party's Over," "Alone 
Together" and "Softly As In A Morning Sun- 
rise." Fine after-hours, moody listening. 
CLASSICAL PICKS 
BEETHOVEN: Quartet No. 15 in A Minor, Op. 
132 - Budapest String Quartet - Columbia MS 
6386 
The Budapest String Quartet comes up with a 
truly majestic reading of Beethoven's famous, 
intricate quartet, on this first-rate classical offer- 
ing from Columbia. The musicians do not rely on 
gimmicks but interpret the somewhat pessimistic 
work in a free -flowing imaginative style paying 
close attention to the difficult, rapidly -changing 
chromatic developments. A collector's item. 
STRAUSS: Arabella, Della Casa, Rothenberger, 
Fischer-Dieskau, Keilberth - Deutsche Grammo- 
phon-SLPM 138 884 
Deutsche Grammophon has rounded up a stellar 
cast of operatic performers for this new produc- 
tion of Richard Strauss's "Arabella." Lisa Della 
Casa, Anneliese Rothenberger, Dietrich Fischer- 
Dieskau, Fritz Uhl sing the principal roles with 
the Bavarian State Opera Orchestra and Chorus 
directed by Joseph Keiberth. Stirring perform- 
ances by the entire cast coupled with the Strauss 
melodies makes the set a worthy addition to the 
opera shelf. Set is brilliant in stereo.

SIDEWALK SURFING!-The Good Guys-GNP 
Crescendo 2001 
The latest "thrill" gimmick comes from the 
Middle -west and is called "Sidewalk Surfing" (a 
surf board with roller skates). The sport is new 
but the accompanying music is in the same tra- 
dition as surfing and hot-rodding. The Good 
Guys lash out with their brand of `sidewalk 
surfing' on this disk from Crescendo-the pattern 
is the same, lots of guitars and a driving beat. 
The kids should take to the sport and the music. 
Included are "Roller Derby," "Small Fry" and 
"Duck Waddle." 
AMERICA'S MOST BELOVED SONGS-Gretl 
Rath-MGM E4236 
Viennese songstress Gretl Rath follows her 
"Vienna Yesterday, Vienna Today" LP with this 
collection of American evergreens from the ar- 
chives of melodic greats. Her wide -range soprano 
and feelingful delivery are perfectly suited to 
"Tonight We Love," "Strange Music," "Till The 
End Of Time" and "And This Is My Beloved." 
The tunes here are a first-rate showcase for her 
talent. Enjoyable listening. 
ENGLAND'S NEW BIG BAND SOUND: THE 
LAURIE JOHNSON ORCHESTRA-Colpix CP 
471 Triple -threat Britisher Laurie Johnson 
(he 
composes, arranges and conducts) sparkles his 
way through a dozen sturdies as he helms his 
big, lush band on this new instrumental offering 
from Colpix. The orkster has created some de- 
lightful fresh, swingin' arrangements of such old 
favorites as "South Of The Border," "My Favor- 
ite Things" and "Pagan Love Song." Fine fare 
for either dancing or listening pleasure. 
CHAD MITCHELL TRIO & THE GATEMAN 
IN CONCERT-Colpix CP 463 
Pop -folk enthusiasts should come out in droves 
for this delightful set showcasing the distinctive 
talents of the Chad Mitchell Trio and the Gate- 
man. The program here runs the gamut from 
popular evergreens to little-known but equally 
interesting "gems." Highlights include "Vaya 
Con Dios," "Green Leaves Of Summer" and "500 
Miles." Deejays should find plenty of program- 
mable material here. 
SURF AGE-Jerry Cole-Capitol ST 2112 
Here's another of Capitol's summer surfin' spe- 
cials with a bonus "piggy -back" 45 rpm deck- 
this time spotlighting the instrumental efforts of 
Jerry Cole and his Spacemen. Cole and crew, who 
captured considerable attention with their first 
LP, "Outer Limits," are sure to get even more 
for this new set which includes hard -driving 
readings of "Surf Age," "Night Rumble," "Jer- 
ry's Jump," and nine other lightning -like items. 
The teen dance crowd will dig it. 
GOLDEN HITS OF HAWAII-Outriggers-War- 
ner Bros. 1549 
Since the days of Captain Cook, Hawaiian 
music has captured the musical fancy of the 
world. The warm, lazy romantic melodies seem 
to suggest the carefree mood of our 50th state. 
The Outriggers, an instrumental sextet, pay a 
moving tribute to Hawaii with this lush program 
of tunes long -associated with the islands. High- 
lights here include "My Isle Of Golden Dreams," 
"Now Is The Hour" and "Hawaiian Wedding 
Song." Nice change -of -pace programming fare. 
MR. & MRS., COUNTRY MUSIC-Joe & Rose 
Lee Máphis-Starday SLP 286 
Joe and Rose Lee Maphis have earned many 
laurels in the past with their distinctive country 
music stylings but this new Starday disk, which 
boasts a fine sampling of traditional items ranks 
as one of their best efforts in quite a while. The 
duo's personal brand of harmony is effectively 
showcased on "I've Come To Take You Home," 
"Lonesome Jailhouse Blues" and "Love Don't 
Live Here Anymore." LP should sell nicely in 
the c&w markets.

THE BEST OF COUNT BASIE-Verve V8596 
Here's the Count Basie band of 1955-56 sparked 
by some of the best musicians in the business, 
along with the potent vocal offerings of Joe 
Williams. The crew swings and rocks throughout 
in rhythmic and tuneful fashion on such bright 
evergreens as "April In Paris," "Alright, O.TX. 
You Win," "One O'Clock Jump" and "In The 
Evening When The Sun Goes Down." Basie - 
Williams fans will want to add this one to their 
shelves.

FANTABULOUS-Oliver Nelson-Argo 737 
Oliver Nelson's stature as a jazzist has been 
growing consistently the last few years and this 
session on Argo does much to add to his, stature. 
Backed by a top-flight crew of sidemen, the tenor 
saxist serves up a lot of soul and feeling here- 
particularly on "Post No Bills," "Three Plus 
One," "Take Me With You" and "Hobo Flats." 
Nelson's approach is middle of the road with 
plenty of universal appeal. 
THE WORD FROM MOSE-Mose Allison-At- 
lantic 1424 
That versatile Mose Allison (he sings in a dis- 
tinctive jazz -blues style and plays a top-notch 
cookin' piano) is back again in a fine program 
of mostly self -penned vocals and midstream in- 
strumentals. While backed by bass and drums 
Allison renders feelingful renditions of "Fool - 
killer," "Look Here" and "I'm Not Talkin'." One 
of the best sets that the artist has cut in quite 
a while. 
MORE GRAVY-Willis Jackson-Prestige PR 
7317 
For those jazzophiles who like their music on 
the hard -driving and cookin' side this new Pres- 
tige outing spotlighting the accomplished tenor 
sax talents of Willis Jackson should be just the 
ticket. Jackson is teamed -up with a first-rate 
crew of jazzmen who blend their distinctive 
talents together into one cohesive musical unit. 
Among the highlights here are "Pool Shark," 
"Somewhere Along The Way" and "More Gravy." 
AM I BLUE-Grant Green-Blue Note 4139 
Ace jazz guitarist Grant Green teams -up with 
an accomplished crew of musicians including 
Johnny Coles (trumpet), Joe Henderson (tenor 
sax) and John Paton (organ) on this moody, 
after-hours set of funky evergreens and original 
bluesers. The group really shines as they turn in 
top-flight renditions of "Take These Chains From 
My Heart," "I Wanna Be Loved" and "For All 
We Know." Superior jazz fare. 
LASSICAL PICKS 
PROKOFIEV: Piano Concertos Nos. 3 & 5 Sam- 
son Francois, pianist; Witold Rowicki conducting 
the Philharmonia Orchestra-Angel S 36193 
Samson Francois reads the two Prokofiev con- 
certi in a commanding lucid style on this top- 
drawer classical entry from Angel. While a lush 
instrumental backing is supplied by Witold Ro- 
wicki, who conducts the Philharmonia Orchestra, 
the pianist goes through the intricate passages, 
which change rapidly from florid slow movements 
to march -like peaks, with an impressive lyrical 
approach. A standout achievement. 
BEETHOVEN: Symphonies No. 8 & No. 4, Min- 
neapolis Symphony/Dorati - Mercury -Wing - 
SRW18042 
Beethoven's lyrical 4th Symphony in B flat 
major and 8th Symphony in F major are per- 
formed by the Minneapolis Symphony with Antal 
Dorati at the helm. Both are brilliantly executed 
under the skillful direction of award -winning 
Dorati. Issued on Mercury's budget -priced label, 
the LP should get considerable sales attention.

LAS VEGAS-Mike Corda, former 
N.Y. tunesmith, now clicking with his 
own Corda pubbery and compositions 
in Vegas, now has seven recordings 
of his "Let's Make The Most Of A 
Beautiful Thing," Sammy Davis, Jr: s 
being the most recent. Other recent 
versions are by John Gary and Adam 
Wade. Corda informed us that Johnny 
Mercer has taken several of his tunes 
with him and expects to pen lyrics 
to them. 
NEW YORK-Millie Small, the 16 - 
year old Jamaican lass who sky- 
rocketed to international fame via her 
ska-introduced Smash decks, "My Boy 
Lollipop" 
and 
"Sweet 
William," 
arrived in New York last week (27) 
for a whirlwind 24 -hour publicity - 
promo visit accompanied by her man- 
ager, Chris Blackwell. 
In the top two photos the young 
lark is shown being welcomed at Ken- 
nedy International Airport by a co- 
terie of New York's Finest. In the 
bottom shots she's pictured receiving 
a huge 'lollipop bouquet' from popular 
WINS deejay, Murray "The K," who 
was on hand for the airport festivities. 
The label kicked -off Millie's trip 
with a cocktail party in the Rainbow 
Room attended by over 150 members 
of the press, Gotham area platter 
spinners, music trade paper reporters 
and official representatives of the 
Jamaican government. 
Eva 
Dolin, Smash's director of 
publicity, made good use of the artist's 
brief stop -over by setting -up several 
interviews with national consumer 
publications. In addition, she arranged 
for extensive radio and television 
coverage. 
Millie returned to her homebase in 
Kingston after her New York sojurn. 
While on the island she will film a 
TV spectacular, "Millie In Jamaica," 
which will be shown in England in 
Oct. and on U.S. screens sometime 
next season. 
A return three-day visit to the 
States for additional press and maga- 
zine interviews has been scheduled 
for August 11th. A special highlight 
of that trip will take place on the 
12th when the New York World's Fair 
honors the songstress with a "Millie 
Small Day," which will include special 
ceremonies throughout the day, be- 
ginning with greetings by City and 
Fair dignitaries.

Victor To Cut "Fiddler" 
NEW YORK-RCA Victor Records 
will record the original -cast LP of 
"Fiddler On The Roof," the musical 
version of Sholem Aleichem's "Tevye" 
stories. With a score by Jerry Bock 
and Sheldon Harnick, the show opens 
on Broadway on Sept. 22, qualifying 
as the first new musical of the 1964- 
65 season. It stars Zero Mostel, who 
got rave reviews for his last Broad- 
way assignment, "A Funny Thing 
." Plans are to record the show 
Sept. 27, under the supervision of 
George Marek, Victor's vp and gen- 
eral manager. 
Jerome Robbins is staging the show 
and doing its choreography. This is 
the first time that a Bock and Har - 
nick show has been cut by Victor. 
Their previous efforts have been re- 
corded by Capitol ("Fiorello!" and 
"Tenderloin") and MGM ("She Loves 
Me") and Columbia (several songs 
for the World's Fair musical, "To 
Broadway With Love"). 
Victor's big cast LP last season 
(and still going strong) was "Hello, 
Dolly!"

Smothers & Mercury Sponsor 
"Slithery Dee" Contest 
NEW YORK-The Smothers Brothers 
and Mercury Records are inviting 
deejays and their listeners to send 
in drawings .of their ideas of a "Slith- 
ery Dee," which is the title of a 
track in their latest LP, "It Must 
Have Been Something I Said." 
The contest idea came from WEZY 
in Cocoa, Florida which asked listen- 
ers to send in their drawings of the 
"Slithery Dee." The response was so 
great, the Smothers and Mercury de- 
cided to make it a national contest 
and award prizes. 
The winner will receive an all ex- 
pense paid trip for two to San Fran- 
cisco 
(Sept. 
17-20) that includes 
round-trip tickets on American Air- 
lines, four nights at the Fairmont 
Rotel, dinner and the Smothers' show 
at the Venetian Room, and a tour of 
the city. The winner's local deejay 
will be given the same prize. Runners 
uP will get prizes varying from Mer- 
cury phonos to Smothers' LP's. 
A toy manufacturer will reproduce 
a replica toy of the winning drawing, 
and give the winner $100 spending 
money for the San Francisco trip. 
The contest is getting heavy na- 
tional promotion, and several draw - 
as 
logs have already been shown on the 
rk

Ray Charles Singers 
To H'wood Bowl 
NEW YORK - Choral director Ray 
Charles and his singers, making big 
singles and LP news for the Com- 
mand label, take time out from their 
busy recording schedule to make an 
appearance this Fri. 
(14) 
at the 
Hollywood Bowl. Concert will also in- 
clude comic Allan Sherman and the 
Hollywood Bowl Orchestra. Before he 
returns east, Charles will make a 
1 -day stopover in Fort Worth to re- 
hearse the Texas Boys' Choir in some 
arrangements he wrote for the en- 
semble. As for the Charles' own crew, 
it's riding high with such singles hits 
as "Love Me With All Your Heart" 
and "Al Di La." 
Mormon Tabernacle Choir 
Gets 2 More Gold Decks 
NEW YORK-Columbia Records has 
awarded 
two 
RIAA-certified 
gold 
disks to 
the Mormon 
Tabernacle 
Choir, each representing album sales 
totaling more than $1 million. The 
disks were awarded last month (26) 
at a presentation ceremony in the 
music hall of the Texas Pavilion at 
the New York World's Fair. 
The awards, given for the choir's 
recordings of Handel's Messiah and 
"The Lord's Prayer," were presented 
to choir president Isaac M. Stewart 
and conductor Richard P. Condie by 
Arthur Hull Hayes, president of CBS 
Radio. 
1st LP Shipment Due 
From Music & Voice 
NEW YORK-Music and Voice Rec- 
ords, new label headed by Art Tal- 
madge, starts shipment of its first 
LP release-consisting of six albums 
-next week (17). 
When the line was introduced to 
distribs at their recent ARMADA 
confab, the company reported orders 
totaling 150,000 albums. Four of the 
albums are part of a "51 Music and 
Voice Series," including "51 Greatest 
Motion Picture Favorites" with the 
Vinnie Bell Orch., "51 Greatest Broad- 
way Favorites" with Milton DeLugg 
and his Orch., with pianist Jon Costa, 
"51 Discotheque Favorites" with Ralph 
Marterie and his Orch. and "51 Or- 
gan Skating Favorites" with George 
Stone at the organ. 
"51 
Series" 
album jackets 
are 
adorned with special pen -and -water 
color artwork by Fred Steffen. 
The other packages are "How To 
Hula At Home" with Sam Makia and 
His Royal Islanders, including 15 fa- 
vorite Hawaiian songs and an instruc- 
tion booklet, and "Music For Isomet- 
ric Exercises," including a book illus- 
trating the exercises published by 
Prentice -Hall. 
Also being shipped by Music and 
Voice is a special package of two 
kiddie play -a -long 45's. The disks 
come with a whistle, cricket, bell and 
coloring card with the lyrics of the 
songs. 
Deutschman Exits 
Decca For Post 
With Orchestra 
NEW YORK - Ben Deutschman has 
resigned his classical post at Decca 
Records to become business manager 
of the Erie, Pennsylvania Philhar- 
monic Orchestra and Chorus. During 
his five year association with Decca, 
the vet music man served as educa- 
tional director of the label, as well 
as publicity and promo director for 
Decca's Gold Label (classical) divi- 
sion. Before joining Decca, he held 
exec posts with Everest, Mercury, 
Capitol and Children's Record Guild.

EXPLANATIONS 
All countries are 
listed in alphabetic 
order. 
All labels listed appears in alphabetic 
order. 
As main addresses appears 
P. 
O. Box 
(English), Apartado 
(Spanish),

Postale 
(French), Postfach 
(German) , 
etc., while street addresses-If known- 
appears within 
( 
). 
Labels (domestic) refer to names of la- 
bels on which are made and released 
local domestic recordings. If any of the 
major labels appears under "domestic," 
it is understood that the company also is 
releasing whatever 
foreign recordings 
there might be available at the same 
label. The name of the label is not re- 
peated under "Labels (others)." 
Labels (others) refer to names of im- 
ported/foreign labels imported by the 
companies under which they are listed. 
Remark: In some countries, mainly Cen- 
tral and South America and Asian coun- 
tries, certain leading retailers have their 
own import from major European and 
American manufacturers, which explain 
why in certain cases certain labels might 
be listed under more than one company 
in each country. 
All informations appearing in this Direc- 
tory originates from the companies them- 
selves, who have listed the informations 
published 
on 
the 
questionnaires they 
have received. 
If and when a certain company is not 
listed in this Directory, it might depend 
upon the fact that the company itself has 
failed 
in 
returning 
the questionnaire 
which has been sent to them. If and 
when so is the case, Cash Box hopes to 
see these companies listed in next year's 
Directory.

England- 
The Past 
Twelve Months 
(Continued from page 34) 
Shapiro 
Bernstein 
have 
counted 
amongst their major hits "I (Who 
Have Nothing)" by Shirley Bassey, 
""White On White" by Danny Williams 
and three Billy Fury numbers "Like 
I've Never Been Gone"; "Do You 
Really Love Me Too" and "In Sum- 
mer" the latter written for him by 
The Avons. The number has also 
been recorded in many countries of 
the world including France where 
it was a very big hit for Claude Fran- 
cois entitled "En Revant A Noel" 
and selling over a half a million 
copies. Another Shapiro Bernstein 
copyright which Francois took into 
the continental charts was ``Every 
Day I Have To Cry." Sidney Bron en- 
joyed a second -time -round hit with 
his "Dance On." Originally an in- 
strumental charter for The Shadows 
it returned to the charts as a vocal 
hit for Kathy Kirby. Bron also had 
an American chart entry via Bobby 
Shafto's single "She's My Girl" pub- 
lished in the States by Lenny Hodes. 
Bron also entered the independent 
recording field by setting up D. B. 
Productions Ltd. headed by Gerry 
Bron and M. D. Syd Dale. Bron also 
won an Ivor Novello Award for The 
Second Most Broadcast Work of the 
Year ``Dance On." Jimmy and Bill 
Philips of K.P.M. after an excellent 
year which included charters such 
as ``Diane" by The Bachelors and 
"`Sweet William" by Millie have just 
had their biggest hit of all with The 
Animals No. 1 charter "The House 
Of The Rising Sun." Sales are now 
getting on for the million mark. 
Harold Geller's newly formed Lynn 
Music got away to a good start with 
"`Johnny Janvier" recorded by Sonny 
Blake on Ember. The number is also 
coming out in Germany where it will 
be published by Minerva and in Italy 
where it is published by Curci. Be- 
sides publishing Geller's activities ex- 
pand into the management and re- 
cording fields. During the year Lionel 
Bart's Apollo Music, under the man- 
agement of Leslie Paul, clinched a 
deal with the Italian publishing house 
of Cielo Girl to handle their copy- 
rights in the U. K. Bart is currently 
pre -occupied putting the finishing 
touches to his latest musical "Mag- 
gie May." Dominion Music and its 
subsidiary companies under the di- 
rection of Noel Rogers has removed 
to new and spacious offices in Knights- 
bridge. During the year his major 
hits have included "Do You Love 
Me" by Brian Poole and the Treme- 
loes and the Aldon copyright "I 
Want To Stay Here" by Steve Law- 
rence and Eydie Gorme. Freddie Poser 
of Poser Music paid his first visit 
to the United States and at home 
enjoyed a visit to chartsville with 
Adam Faith's "The First Time" and 
"We Are In Love." Last but not least 
he had a big hit with Gene Pitney's 
"`That Girl Belongs To Yesterday." 
Marquis Music came up with their 
first chart entry "Not Too Little 
Not Too Much" by actor/singer Chris 
Sandford. Marquis also entered art- 
ist/management the first signing be- 
ing The Zombies who have recorded 
for Decca. The Phoenix group of com- 
panies also entered into artist/man- 
agement. Their first signing being a 
group called The U.K's who record 
for Columbia. Mellin Music had a 
long and sustained hit with ``Twist 
And Shout" and Essex Music ac- 
quired 
an 
equal partnership 
in- 
terest in the publishing houses of 
Jazz Music Ltd. 
and Key Music 
Ltd. owned by Johnny Dankworth. 
Essex had a major hit with "If 
I Had A Hammer" by Trini Lopez. 
The Lorna Music group expanded with 
the formation of three new companies, 
Woodside Music, Laurel Music and 
Trident. Lorna Music was founded 
four years ago on behalf of Wilhelm 
Jansen (Denmark). Leeds Music has 
once again enjoyed continued chart 
success with the Cliff Richard hits 
in the catalogue of their subsidiary 
Elstree Music. The latest being "On 
The Beach "from his "Wonderful Life" 
movie. In the same group Welbeck 
Music had two hits by The Search- 
ers ``Don't Throw Your Love Away" 
and "Sugar and Spice." Aberbach 
went to the top with Cilla Black's 
"You're My World" and Belinda (Lon- 
don) climed high with "Little Chil- 
dren" by Billy J. Kramer and "Wish - 
in' And Hoping" by The Merseybeats 
in England and Dusty Springfield in 
the United States. Jack Mills paid 
his annual and welcome visit to Eng- 
land. 
A commendable transatlantic 
hook-up has been established by Am- 
bassador Music London and Gil Pincus 
America. A hands -across -the -sea ex- 
change of material has paid handsome 
dividends-The Beatles for Gil Pincus 
and The Surfaris "Wipe Out" for 
Ambassador, who continue to enjoy 
the sweet smell of success with "A 
Taste Of Honey." And on that anglo - 
American note we close Great Bri- 
tain's annual review for the year 
1963/1964.

SWITZERLAND-The Past 12 Months 
(Continued from page 130) 
also enjoyed good sales in Switzer- 
land.. Artistes who have appeared in 
Switzerland with considerable success 
include Casadesus, Brailowsky, Fran- 
cescatti and Percy Faith. Phonag have 
recently acquired the Saba label of 
Germany. 
Anton and Jane Peterer of Edition 
Melodie and Edition Coda of Zurich 
have obtained the distribution rights 
of the new Pick label which they will 
launch in September with a catalogue 
of ten L.Ps including new titles by 
jazz -guitarist Pierre Cavalli. Coda 
handled the winning song from the 
1964 Baden-Baden Festival "Liebe- 
skummer Lohnt Sich Nicht" by Siv 
Malmkwist. To cope with the growing 
demand for background music Coda 
have recorded 
14 South American 
titles especially for radio and televi- 
sion. Furthermore, Coda controls all 
music from the Swiss films released 
by Urania -Film. 
The newly formed Flora musikver- 
lag in Uster got off to a good start 
with "Drei Musketiere" by Conny 
Froebus on Electrola and "Wenn Ich 
Ein Junge War" by Italian star Rita 
Pavone. 
Editions Helbling of Zurich were 
the publishers of Switzerland's entry 
in the Eurovision Song Contest "I 
Mieu Pensieri" (My Thoughts). 
Over the past four or five years 
Switzerland's most important distrib- 
utors have noticed 
a 
steady but 
marked increase in the sales of classi- 
cal music and happily report that this 
is not only confined to the older gen- 
eration of record buyers. The teen- 
agers, too, are becoming classical 
minded. A top seller for Musikver- 
trieb ever since 1961 has been the 
celebrated international pianist Van 
Cliburn. Also popular in the classical 
field are recordings by Wilhelm Back- 
haus. 
Editions Sidem enjoyed a string of 
hits 
by 
top 
American, 
English, 
French, German and Italian stars in- 
cluding Trini Lopez, The Beatles, 
Charles Aznavour, Gitte and Rex 
Gildo and Adriano Celentano. Sister 
company, Mondiamusic is primarily 
engaged in handling film scores from 
leading continental films. 
To sum up Switzerland is a very 
music conscious nation with a public 
taste which ranges from pop and jazz 
to classics. During the past year 
Switzerland 
has 
welcomed 
many 
world famous artistes including The 
Modern Jazz Quarter, Oscar Petersen, 
Humphrey Lyttelton, Duke Ellington, 
Paul Anka, The Thelonious 
Monk 
Quartet, The Max Roach Quartet, The 
Red Army Choir and many top Ger- 
man variety shows, all of whom have 
been very warmly received. 
Yes, Switzerland really is a land of

SWEDEN 
1963 
The sale of records in Sweden dur- 
ing 1963 shows an increase of 169,792 
records more than during 1962. The 
majority of the increase was LP's 
which also means that it did not add 
much profit to the trade itself, since 
it was mainly the record -like sale of 
the UNO record "All Star Festival" 
that was responsible for the increase. 
The sales figures show a total sale 
of 
3,872,341 
(against 
3,862,493) 
singles and EP's in 1963-an increase 
of 9848 records, and 865,824 (against 
705,880) LP's in 1963. However, of 
the LP's, 169,400 of them were the 
"All Star Festival." Deducting the 
sale of this record from the statistics, 
it is obvious that the LP sale in 
Sweden in 1963 dropped with not less 
than 9456 items compared with the 
year before. It can't, of course, be es- 
timated how many people would have

bought other LP's if the UNO record 
had not been available, but on the 
other hand, it is obvious that a lot 
of people who usually never bought 
any LP, did so for the first time when 
the UNO record was offered to them. 
Chances are that those people be- 
came future LP customers, something 
that in the long run will help to add 
profit for the trade. 
Biggest profit of 1963 went to the 
government, which collected not less 
that 5,961,613 Kronor in luxury taxes 
for records sold. It is a sum corres- 
ponding to $1,192,322. This luxury 
tax is one Krona (20¢) for singles 
or EP's and three Kronor (60e) on 
LP's. The government collected its 
luxury tax also for the UNO record, 
but this money was handed over to 
the UNO by the government. 
There is at the present a new tax 
system being investigated by the au- 
thorities. This includes among others 
that records (and several other things 
on which there are heavy luxury tax- 
es) should be tax free. The record 
trade here has promised that if the 
government withdraws its taxes on 
records, prices on the same will drop 
with sums corresponding to the taxes.

Sweden's Tape Recorde 
STOCKHOLM-Each year, some 60,- 
000 new tape recorders find their way 
to buyers in Sweden, writes Dr. Sven 
Wilson, head 
of STIM 
(Sweden's 
ASCAP) in a small booklet titled 
"Pa Begäran" (Upon Request). 
It is no secret that those tape re- 
corders are to blame when speaking 
about the drop in sales figures from 
all record companies, 
Dr. Wilson 
thinks. 
If a group of ten teenagers buys 
ten tape recorders, they will not buy 
ten records with their idols. They buy 
one record at the most. Often, they 
don't buy any records at all. They 
hear it on radio and tape it. 
According to Dr. Wilson, the au- 
thorities were aware of this problem 
when the present Copyright Law was 
written in 1956, but it wasn't judged 
too much of a problem at that time. 
But since then, the sales of tape re- 
corders have increased enormously, 
and suddenly it has become a prob- 
lem. According to Wilson, it is obvi- 
ous that the authorities must find 
r Problem 
one or another way to solve the prob- 
lem, which becomes more and more 
gigantic, with less and less phono- 
graph records sold as a result. 
As a comment to the above, it can 
be mentioned that various solutions 
of this problem have been mentioned 
from time to time. One of these solu- 
tions is that each owner of a tape re- 
corder should be registered and pay 
a certain sum each year, something 
like the licenses for having radios or 
TV. The money coming in from those 
licenses on tape recorders would be 
used to compensate record manufac- 
turers for their losses, another part 
to compensate composers/authors for 
their loss, etc. 
Dr. 
Wilson 
writes that STIM 
reached a peak of 9,500,000 Kronor 
in 1963 against 7,500,000 Kronor in 
1962 ($1,900,000 against $1,500,000). 
About 5 per cent of the money came 
from radio and TV. STIM does not 
collect any mechanical licenses. It is 
a Performing Rights Society only.

DENMARK'S BEST SELLERS 
As in the other Scandinavian countries, The Beatles ended up as the top sell- 
ing artists of the first six months of 1964. Denmark was also the only Scandi- 
navian country who got a visit by the famous group. 
Local copyrights had its chance at the Danish market in April, when Den- 
mark's Eurovision Song Contest entry "Sangen om dig" (The Song Of You), 
and the song ending at second spot in the Danish local Song Festival, "Det er 
en forskel" (It is A Difference), held the first and second spot in the charts.

NORWAY'S BEST SELLERS 
Norway has got its share of The Beatles, at least on records, during 1964. 
However, local copyrights has done very good, too, particularly thanks to rec- 
ord -breaking nightingale Wenche Myhre, who did it with "La meg vere ung" 
(Let Me Be Young) on Triola, topping the charts two months, and among the 
Top 10 for more than four months. Also the satirical "Dagligliv i Folkehjem- 
met" (Daily Life In The Welfare Country), a Norwegian "The First Family" 
appeared among the top three.

FINLAND-The 
As a record market, Finland is or 
at least has been a country where 
Finnish -language records never had 
any trouble competing with foreign 
language recordings. Finland is also 
the market where domestic copyrights 
usually dominate the charts. 
However, this might come to an end 
as Finland seems to be becoming a 
teenager's market, and for some rea- 
sons, teenagers seem unlikely to "ac- 
cept" their own language on records- 
at least in Scandinavia. So far, any- 
how, with the exception of the Beatles, 
a Finnish version of a record with, 
for example, Elvis Presley, is doing 
better than the original one. A good 
example of this is "Seinillä on korvat" 
with Eino Grön on Scandia, a Finnish 
version of "The Walls Have Ears". 
The Elvis Presley version did not cre- 
ate much noise at the Finnish market, 
but the local version was on the charts 
for at least three months. 
Also, popular songs sung by the 
Beatles, have been recorded in Finnish 
with good results, but in those cases, 
the original versions have been taking 
the big money.

Swiss Inventor Unveils 
New Record Changer 
NEW YORK-A new record changer 
was unveiled here last week (10), the 
Discomatic, which can play up to 40 
seven-inch disks on both sides con- 
tinuously with no other action re- 
quired after the initial selection of 
records is made. 
The result of seven and one half 
years of research and development 
by inventor M. Jean Foufounis, presi- 
dent of the Swiss Gerinvex firm, the 
Discomatic permits greater freedom 
of selection and longevity of play 
than has ever before been possible 
in any moderate -cost home phono. In 
addition, after a program of tunes 
has been selected, any one or all can 
be cancelled or changed at any time 
during play by merely pushing and/ 
or pulling the selector buttons or 
totally rejecting them all via one 
master switch. 
The Discomatic consists of three 
major components: a stationary base 
and push button system, a traveling 
disk selector and playing arm assem- 
bly driven by a small electric motor, 
and a high impact styrene plastic 
record rack with the 40 -disk capacity. 
The rack is removable and another 
can be put into its place. Each disk 
slot 
is numbered 
with numbered 
sheets supplied for each rack, and 
the number of the disk playing lights 
up for easy reference. The changer 
will play 45 or 33 and 1/3 RPM rec- 
ords by manual or automatic control, 
depending upon the model. 
American disk and phono manu- 
facturers previewed the Discomatic 
at the St. Regis Hotel here prior to 
its being exhibited at the Interna- 
tional Radio Show in London this 
month (28). 
Designer Foufounis said the ma- 
chine would retail initially at a cost 
of under $200, and that the cost 
would drop considerably as produc- 
tion expanded. 
Light, Lombardo Named 
Among 10 Best Dressed 
NEW YORK-Enoch Light, manag- 
ing director of Command Records, 
and maestro Guy Lombardo have been 
named among the best dressed men 
in America by the Fashion Founda- 
tion of America. 
Light was selected by the Fashion 
Foundation for the second year in a 
row. Two years ago he was picked by 
the Custom Tailors of America on 
their best dressed list. 
The latest best dressed selections 
listed Light in the recording category. 
Top dresser in the music field was 
Guy Lombardo, while Sydney Chap- 
lin, star of Broadway's "Funny Girl" 
topped the stage category. Glenn Ford 
won in the movie category. 
Others included in the list were 
President Johnson, Barry Goldwater, 
Mayor Robert Wagner, Jack Dempsey, 
Robert W. Sarnoff, chairman of NBC, 
and O. Wayne Rollins, president of 
Rollins 
Broadcasting, 
Wilmington, 
Del.

CIRCUS WORLD-Original Soundtrack-MGM 
E425ST 
Dimitri Tiomkin's score for the new Cinerama 
production, "Circus World," is a three-ring circus 
of melody in itself. The composer has effectively 
captured the flavor of the circus with a host of 
original melodies into which have been inter- 
woven a continental flavor that coincides with 
the plot development. The much -heralded Bron- 
ston flick is reportedly doing top box-office busi- 
ness and the soundtrack album could do likewise. 
THE GOOD GUYS SING-United Artists UAL 
3370 
The Good Guys, the deejays of WMCA-New 
York, step outside their roles of platter spinners 
and unleash their potent vocal talents full -blast 
on this swingin' teen -angled set from United 
Artists. The six air personalities offer infectious 
renditions of "Hello, Dolly," "Heart" and "For 
Me And My Gal." Could become a giant chart - 
rider. 
EVERYBODY'S DOING IT-Vol.'s 1, 2 & 3- 
Bobby Jay & Hawks-Warner Bros. 1562 
Teenage dancers as well as their parents should 
really dig this three -volume set of contemporary 
"in" dances spotlighting the infectious instru- 
mental talents of Bobby Jay and the Hawks. The 
series includes a watusi, ska and monkey album. 
Among the standout tracks here are "Louie, 
Louie," "Monkey Time" and "Ska Time." Con- 
sumers will want all three disks. 
TURNING IT ON !-Gaslight Singers-Mercury 
SR 60923 
The Gaslight Singers, who have recently been 
building a national reputation for themselves via 
their club shots, come up with their second album 
in the pop -folk idiom. The crew does not attempt 
to carbon -copy other groups but runs through 
their varied repertoire in a distinctive, fresh - 
sounding style which tastefully blends harmony 
and counterpoint. Best listening bets here in- 
clude "This Life I'm Living," "By The Bay Of 
Pigs" and "They Call The Wind Maria." 
WOODY HERMAN'S GOLDEN FAVORITES- 
Decca DL 74484 
Here's a nostalgic package of pop -jazz ever- 
greens which have become associated with Woody 
Herman over the years. The vet orkster-clarinet- 
ist, who wrote _a large sampling of tunes here 
himself, cut the set during his days with Decca._. 
The large, lush Herman band turns in top-drawer 
renditions of "Woodchopper's Bail," "The Golden 
Wedding" and "Blue Flame." Deejays should find

This new Colpix disk is indeed worthy of spe-

THE DEFINITIVE JAZZ SCENE-Various Art- 
ists-Impulse A-99 
Jazz collectors should come out in droves for 
this top-notch Impulse set which features a 
stellar coterie of artists dishing -up a splendid 
program of rare and previously unreleased re- 
cordings. The LP spans the entire gamut of the 
modern jazz idiom going all the way from the 
far-out sounds of Charlie Mingus to the com 
paratively conservative Duke Ellington progres- 
sions. Loads of airplay potential here.

Victor LPV 506 
Jazzophiles should come out in force for this 
extremely interesting set of jazz classics featur-

some of them never previously released, were cut 
by the orkster between June '31 and May '34. 
There's plenty of nostalgic listening as the crew 
offers "Limehouse Blues," "It's Glory" and "Blue 
Feeling." A real collector's item.

Herman Writing Score 
For Musical "Mame," 
Starring Mary Martin 
NEW YORK-The fall of 1965 will 
witness a new Broadway score by 
Jerry ("Hello, Dolly!") Herman, part 
of which will be sung by Mary 
Martin. 
Production will be a musical ver- 
sion of "Auntie Mame," with a book 
by Jerome Lawrence and Robert E. 
Lee, who wrote the legit version of 
Patric Dennis' book. Original "Mame" 
producers, Robert Fryer and Law- 
rence Carr, original producers of the

put on the show in partnership with

No original -cast label has been an- 
nounced. 
Col Pacts Lyn Roman 
NEW YORK-Columbia Records has 
signed vocalist Lyn Roman to an ex- 
clusive disk contract, according to 
Ken Glancy, vice president of A&R. 
Born in Washington, D.C., the 21 - 
year -old performer began her profes- 
sional career at the age of 11 when 
she, two sisters and a brother formed 
a gospel -singing group called the 
Heavenly Stars. Four years later, she 
debuted as a soloist at Washington's 
Koko Club and went on to perform in 
the Capitol's Lotus Club, Champagne 
Room, Casino Royal and The Place 
on the Hill. She studied voice at 
Howard University. 
Her debut Columbia album, "The 
Many Faces Of Lyn Roman," was di- 
rected by Clyde Otis, pop A&R pro- 
ducer for Columbia, and is scheduled 
for release in Sept. 
Stations' Harmonica Promo 
To Follow Beatles' U.S. Tour 
NEW YORK-When the Beatles make 
their coast -to -coast tour, beginning 
Aug. 19, they'll find their way lined 
with harmonicas. 
Radio stations along their itinerary 
have been flocking to join M. Hohner's 
Beatles harmonica promo, designed to 
publicize the Beatles' connection with 
the harmonica. 
New York's WMCA is giving away 
harmonicas as prizes in an eight -day 
promotion. They'll be awarded at half- 
hour intervals throughout the day to 
winners of Beatles slogan contests. 
WBZ's Jefferson Kaye has taken 
to playing the harmonica on his show 
in preparation for the Boston sta- 
tion's promo, to be staged by its Beach 
Boy Club. 
WLBJ, Bowling Green, Ky., will be 
broadcasting from a Beatle booth at 
the Kentucky State Fair, and will 
award harmonicas to listeners chosen 
from those registering at the booth. 
In Atlantic City, N.J., WMID will 
award harmonicas in on -the -air pro- 
mos and at teenage record hops. 
Other stations that have joined the 
promo to date are: KLIF, Dallas; 
WAPE, Jacksonville, Fla.; WBAY, 
Green Bay, Wis.; WIBC, Indianapolis; 
WIBG, 
Philadelphia; 
and 
KFWB, 
Los Angeles, WSAI, Cincinnati; and 
WTIX, New Orleans.

Sharp June Upswing In 
'at
Distrib, Factory Phono Sales 
WASHINGTON - Both distrib and 
factory sales of portable/table and 
console model phonos climbed sharply 
in June, bringing year-to-date totals 
near or beyond those of last year, ac- 
cording to figures from the Electronic 
Industries Association. 
Distrib 
sales 
of 
portable/table 
phonos totaled 217,171 in June, com- 
pared to 136,669 in May. A total of 
989,010 units were sold in the first six 
months of this year, compared 
to 
1,122,757 for the comparable period 
last year. There were 215,036 port- 
able/table models sold in June 1963. 
Distrib sales of consoles totaled 
126,026 units in June, compared to 
70,682 in May. There were 658,335 
consoles sold during the January -June 
period this year, against 636,745 
in 
1963. In June 1963 there were 100,007 
units sold. 
Factory sales 
of 
portable/table 
models totaled 310,742 in June, com- 
pared to 132,959 in May. The total 
for the first six months was 1,047,190, 
against 1,191,326 for the same period 
last year. There were 305,946 units 
sold in June 1963.

at the factory during June, compared 
to 70,936 in May. Six-month totals 
were 656,819 in 1964 and 702,972 in 
1963. There were 149,253 units sold in 
June 1963.

auto) totaled 4,019,448 in the Jan - 
June period, compared to 3,935,670 in 
1963. There were 811,923 radios sold 
last June, with total radio production 
reaching 1,770,884, compared to 1,410; 
660 in May. Six month totals were 
8,939,238, compared to 8,585,238 
in 
1963. There were 1,653,866 radios pro- 
duced in June, 1963.

GUNFIGHT AT O. K. CORRAL-Walter Bren- 
nan-Liberty LRP 3372 
Walter Brennan pays a moving tribute to the 
Old West on this Liberty set of popular recent 
vintage tunes associated with the cowboy life. 
While backed by a rich chorus, the vet thespian 
talks his way through "Riders In The Sky," 
"Cool Water" and "High Noon" with loads of 
sincerity and verve. Delightful listening throug- 
out. 
MORE PRETTY GIRLS THAN ONE-Casey An- 
derson-Atco 33-166 
Casey Anderson could well establish a national 
reputation for himself with this top-notch pop - 
folk -blues set from Atco. The chanter -guitarist 
has a powerful, rich, wide -range baritone voice 
and a distinctive, talkin' blues delivery. The ma- 
terial here runs the gamut from "recently -written 
message songs to traditional evergreens. Among 
the best bets are "More Pretty Girls Than One," 
"This Little Light Of Mine" and "Bury Me In 
My Shades." 
THAT'S ALL-Haymes-Mundy Orchestra -20th 
Century -Fox TFM 3142 
Jimmy Mundy and Bob Haymes combine their 
distinctive musical talents and join forces in their 
own 40 -piece orchestra on this easy-going instru- 
mental set of mostly Haymes-penned tunes from 
20th Century Fox. There's plenty of fine dancing 
and/or listening pleasure as the orksters dish -up 
sophisticated arrangements of "The Fox," "I'll 
Teach You How To Cry" and "Curtain Time." 
TV'S "PENNY" ROSEMARY PRINZ SINGS- 
Pharos MN 10001 
Rosemary Prinz, one of the stars of CBS-TV'er 
daytimer, "As The World Turns," makes an aus- 
picious recording debut with this fine set of chest- 
nuts and recent vintage items. The thespian has 
a lyrical legit -styled voice and a dramatic, power - 
packed delivery. She shines on "Always," "When 
I Fall In Love" and "My Coloring Book." A 
talent to watch. 
THE SONGS WE HEARD WHEN WE WERE 
IN FRANCE-London International SW 99334 
Here is a bit of nostalgia from London Inter- 
national that recalls the era immediately follow- 
ing WW II in France and the melodies played by 
Frenchmen for the thousands of American sol- 
diers waiting to go home. Coupled with these 
songs, played by the orchestra of Maurice Lar - 
cange, are the everyday sounds heard on the 
streets of Paris. The songs are lilting and ro- 
mantic and loaded with Gallic charm. "La Java 
Bleue," "Les Bourgeois," "La Chaloupee" and "La 
Cuisine" are just a few. 
THE LITTLE SINGERS OF TOKYO ON TOUR 
-Request SRLP 8055 
The Little Singers of Tokyo make their Ameri- 
can wax debut on Request with this set of Japa- 
nese tunes. The youngsters, who recently won 
wide critical acclaim for their American concert 
tour, offer the musical highlights of that tour- 
folk tunes devised over the years and delight- 
fully delivered by this mixed choir. Included here 
are "Moon On The Ruins," "Where Are You?" 
"Song On The Beach" and others. Pleasant listen- 
ing throughout. 
THE FREEDOM SINGERS SING OF FREE- 
DOM NOW!-Mercury SR 60924 
Civil rights looms as a prime target for docu- 
mentary albums and Mercury gets the ball roll- 
ing with this entry of freedom songs and spoken 
word offerings. The civil rights movement has 
been fraught with tragedy and sorrow, and it is 
this sorrow that the Freedom Singers tell of in 
song and word. A moving speech by John Lewis 
is included with "We Are Soldiers In The Army," 
"They . Laid Medgar Evers In His Grave" and 
many others. The set is sure to stir up plenty 
of sales attention. 
THE SIDEWINDER 
LEE MORGAN 
JAll PICKS 
MILES DAVIS IN EUROPE-Columbia CL 2183 
The Newport Jazz Festival's European counter- 
part is the festival at Antibes and this new jazz 
romp on Columbia recalls some of the brighter 
moments of last year's meet and in particular 
the trumpet of Miles Davis. Introduced at this 
festival was drummer Tony Williams who's heard 
on this session along with tenor saxist George 
Coleman. The trumpeter is in top form as he 
offers "Milestones," "Autumn Leaves," "Joshua," 
"All Of You" and "Walkin'." The jazz purists 
will dig this set. 
LIVE AT THE LIVING ROOM-Three Sounds 
-Mercury SR 60921 
The Three Sounds, those doyens of middle-of- 
the-road jazz melodies, are back again in a live 
setting, this set having been cut at Cincinnati's 
Living Room. The trio's straight -forward distinc- 
tive brand of harmony and counterpoint are ef- 
fectively showcased on "Mississippi Mud," "Once 
In A Lifetime" and "Glory Of Love." Disk seems 
sure to pull plenty of loot. 
A MUSICAL AUTOBIOGRAPHY OF LOUIS 
ARMSTRONG 1930-34-Decca DL 74331 
Here's a nostalgic set of jazz oldies cut by 
Louis Armstrong during his days with Decca. 
These Depression tunes have all become firmly 
established with Satchmo over the past three dec- 
ades and the vet trumpeter -singer turns in top- 
drawer renditions of "Body And Soul," "You 
Rascal You" and "Them There Eyes." A collec- 
tor's item. 
A JAZZ PORTRAIT OF JACK LA FORGE- 
Regina R 314 
The jazz side of the La Forge coin is deftly 
showcased on this new album outing from Re- 
gina. The 88'er, with a string of successful pop 
albums to his credit, exhibits a flair for the jazz 
idiom ashe essays a dozen standards and origi- 
nals in a feelingful and inventive manner. Loads 
of good listening and choice programming to be 
had here as the pianist reads through such de - 
lighters as "Like Young," "Blues On Velvet," 
"But Not For Me" and "Summertime." Brisk 
sales seem assured. 
JAll BEST BET 
THE SIDEWINDER-Lee Morgan-Blue Note 
4157 
Ace jazz trumpeter Lee Morgan teams -up with 
a top-flight crew of sidemen on this new Blue 
Note date including Joe Henderson (tenor sax), 
Barry Harris (piano), Bob Cranshaw (bass) and 
Billy Higgins (drums). While backed by the 
above -mentioned combo Morgan constructs some 
imaginative, midstream melodic variations 
on 
"The Sidewinder," "Gary's Notebook" and "Boy, 
What A Night." Loads of potential here.

GROFE: Grand Canyon Suite; Leonard Bernstein 
conducting the New York Philharmonic-Colum- 
bia-ML 6018 
Leonard Bernstein departs from his recent 
usual traditional classical context and directs the 
New York Philharmonic in a sweeping, full- 
bodied reading of 
Grofe's three -decades 
old 
"Grand Canyon Suite." The conductor injects all 
of the necessary orchestral "bigness" to work 
and completely captures the majesty and spirit 
of the suite's bucolic flavor. A standout recording. 
MAHLER: Symphony No. 5, Boston Symphony/ 
Leinsdorf-RCA Victor LM 7031 
Here's an attractively boxed two -disk set from 
Victor that includes Mahler's fifth symphony In 
C -sharp minor in its entirety plus excerpts from 
Berg's Wozzeck. The program is performed by 
the Boston Symphony Orchestra with Erich 
Leinsdorf at the helm. The Wozzeck excerpts fea- 
ture Phyllis Curtin as soprano soloist with the 
Sacred Heart Boychoir of Roslindale, Mass. Both 
works are brilliantly executed and merit the at- 
tention of the classical devotee.

Gale Garnett 
Gale 
Garnett, who is currently 
zooming up the charts with her RCA 
Victor recording of "We'll Sing In 
The Sunshine," was born in Auck- 
land, New Zealand, the eldest daugh- 
ter of an English carnival pitchman 
and a Russian emigre. When Gale 
was nine, the family left the South 
Pacific for America. They travelled 
throughout the nation before event- 
ually coming to New York. 
A few years later Gale's father 
died and she took her own apartment 
on Gotham's lower East Side and she 
opted for a career in show business. 
Gale made her professional debut as 
an actress when she was fifteen. 
Three years afterwards her high 
school career ended when she landed 
a role in the touring cbmpany of "The 
Drunkard." As a thespian she pro- 
ceeded to be featured in no less than 
forty-five TV shows. In 1960 a flick 
part brought her to Paris where she 
remained for a while after its com- 
pletion soaking up Gallic culture. 
When she returned to the U. S. she 
made her singing debut at Los Ange- 
les' Garret. The debut was successful 
and was soon followed by club dates 
in key spots across the country and 
her first Victor LP, "My Kind of 
Folk Songs." She's been a full-time 
singer ever since. 
Brian Poole & Tremeloes 
Brian Poole and the Tremeloes, 
after a bevy of triumphs in their na- 
tive England, are scoring stateside 
with "Someone, Someone" 
on the 
Monument label. 
Brian was born twenty-three years 
ago in Barking, Essex. As a child he 
showed an early interest in music 
and, encouraged by his parents, took 
five years of lessons with a private 
tutor. After the completion of his 
studies, Brian began a singing career 
when he was nineteen years old. In 
1960 the young hopeful teamed with 
a four -strong group of musicians and 
singers who 
called themselves the 
Tremeloes. The boys' fortunes soon 
took a turn for the better. 
In rapid-fire fashion they hit the 
charts with "Twist And Shout," "Do 
You Love Me," "Candy Man," etc., 
and found themselves in a spotlight 
of attention. Since then the group has 
played engagements all over Europe 
plus South Africa and New Zealand. 
They've also made two films together.
